LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. Who wll win this time? | Getty Images Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants and Washington Commanders kick off Week 10 of the NFL season Thursday night at what promises to be a rainy, chilly MetLife Stadium. Can the Giants solidify their NFC East lead, or will the race for the division title tighten? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the Week 10 matchups. Which version of the Giants will show up on Thursday night? Will we get the sloppy Giants that came out flat against the Philadelphia Eagles, or the tough, physical, and technically sound Giants that showed up against the Houston Texans? John Harbaugh's 9-1 record home record on Thursday Nights is encouraging. I would say that this is a game the Giants should win on paper, particularly with Washington missing some of their best players and their starting center in the concussion protocol. However, I'm also not convinced that these Giants can play a normal game and just take care of business. I keep waiting for the Giants to play a complete game and execute on offense and defense, but this team seems unable to be both consistent and explosive. I hope the offensive line comes prepared to bully an injured Washington defensive line and J.J. McCarthy isn't forced into low percentage throws every third down by long yardage situations. Likewise, I hope that Dennard Wilson comes out swinging on defense, but also has a counterpunch ready in case Jayden Daniels has an answer to the Cover-0 blitz. I'm picking the Giants here, but they can't afford to take Washington lightly or give Jayden Daniels the chance to catch his breath and swing the game. Tony Del Genio This is the Giants' second consecutive must-win game. You wouldn't think that when 5-2-1 plays 2-5-1, but (1) the Giants haven't beaten the Commanders since Jayden Daniels became their quarterback (even though Daniels didn't play in one of those losses), (2) despite their record, Washington has beaten the Seahawks and only narrowly lost to the 49ers and Rams while the Giants were beaten soundly by the Rams, the only good team they've faced, and still have the 49ers and Seahawks coming up, along with the Jaguars and Lions. A division loss greatly weakens their hold on the NFC East lead, their only real path to the playoffs. Terry McLaurin is out for the season, but in his place is Stefon Diggs, who did not face the Giants in the first game. Jacory Crosky-Merritt, who beat the Giants' run D for a 33-yard TD right off the bat in the first game, is also out. The Commanders are further decimated by injuries since their last meeting to key starters such as DT Daron Payne and IOL Lucas Patrick. So really the Giants should prevail. The problem is…containing the running of Daniels, which they did not do well in their first meeting (103 yards, by far his highest of the season, and his only 2 rushing TDs of the season). Hopefully Dennard Wilson will have a plan for that. If so, and if the Giants execute it, then the Giants can win. David Hartman The rematch of the NFL's only tie game of the season will be played in prime time on Thursday night, and for the ninth time in nine games, the Giants are playing a team that doesn't have a winning record. But you can throw the records out the window: The 5-2-1 Giants, at home, are just 1.5 point favorites over the 2-5-1 Commanders. Go figure… Big Blue won with defense and a strong kicking game on Sunday in Philadelphia, with Arvel Reese perhaps becoming a star in real time. It was an ugly win, with the offense producing just 19 points. The Giants will need more than that against Jayden Daniels and company on Thursday night. Cam Skattebo is expected back, and that's good news. New York couldn't run the ball on Sunday, which stagnated their offense. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) might miss this game, however, and the O-line struggled at Philadelphia as it was. J.J. McCarthy wasn't terrible on Sunday, but he wasn't especially good either and now he's dealing with a hip pointer. Jameis Winston led New York on its only touchdown drive while McCarthy was temporarily knocked from the game. McCarthy hasn't thrown a TD pass (or an interception) in either of his two starts. This figures to be a close game, just like the first one. It'll be fun to watch standout rookies Reese and Sonny Styles — college teammates at Ohio State last season — leading the way for each defense. Seriously – how did anyone score on the Buckeyes? Anyway, Dennard Wilson needs to find a way to keep Daniels from gashing his defense with his legs. He ran for 103 yards and two scores in the first game. This game could come down to intangibles like turnovers and special teams. The G-Men have been winning (or tying) close games and that's a reflection on good coaching to a degree, and favorable luck. In a game that should be close, who am I to pick against that? Pick: Giants in a squeaker Valentine's View We are not picking games by the spread here, but I am surprised the Giants are just 1.5-point favorites. That indicates a continuing lack of real belief in the Giants in the betting market. The Giants understand the opportunity they have in front of them, and how important this game is. In the rainy, windy, miserable conditions at MetLife Stadium Thursday evening I think you have to expect what has become a typical Giants game this season — close, somewhat sloppy, decided by who makes the plays and who properly handles the situations at the end of the game. I have far more faith in the Giants to do that than I do the Commanders. We all remember the Commanders stunning clock mismanagement at the end of the Week 5 tie with the Giants. That sort of questionable decision-making has continued to plague Washington, which is 1-3-1 in games decided by one score. If you could the Arizona game, which I do since it was decided on the game's final play, seven of the Giants eight games this season were one-score games. The Giants are 5-1-1 in those games. They have lived on the edge, and have shown an ability to survive. Is that formula sustainable forever? Maybe not. It does, though, make me feel good about the Giants' chances on Thursday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch the game Imagn Images The New England Patriots and Detroit Lions are headed to Germany this week. The teams will kick off Sunday's action with a 9:30 a.m. game at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins . The victory extended their win streak to four games. Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings . The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers . In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11). The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East. Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to know Injuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Patriots defense got embarrassed last week, with arguably Christian Gonzalez's worst game of his career. New England's defense has allowed the eighth most passing yards per game (231.9). The team does significantly better against the run, landing eighth-best (96.7), right behind the Lions' run defense (94.1). The Lions offense is top 10 in the league, thanks to Jaymyr Gibbs, who already has 847 yards on the ground and will present a challenge for the Patriots. The Lions' pass defense is still at the bottom in terms of yards allowed (260.9), and with the Patriots needing to improve and establish their air game, this would be the chance to try and expose Detroit's weakness. Pass game: The Patriots' passing game pales in comparison to their Week 10 opponent's. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has 61 receptions for 657 receiving yards, more than the Patriots' top two WRs ( DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism III ) combined. The lack of production is in part due to struggles from quarterback Drake Maye and the absence of a true WR1, with Brown missing most games and the loss of Kayshon Boutte this offseason. St. Brown's mom is from Germany and it will be the first game he plays on German soil, which should only increase his excitement and production. International history: This marks the sixth regular-season game to be held in Germany and the third played in Munich. It marks the final European game of the season. The NFL traveled to Germany last season as well, when the Colts and Falcons met in November at the Olympic Stadium. Detroit Lions president & CEO Rod Wood expressed his excitement to be playing in Germany, saying , "We are thrilled to be playing internationally and specifically in Munich for the 2026 season. As an organization, we have invested greatly in the German market and are excited to play in front of our passionate German fans." Lions vs. Patriots where to watch Date: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location : Allianz Arena (Munich, Germany) TV: Fox | Stream: fubo (free trial available) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Lions -2.5 ( via DraftKings ) Lions vs. Patriots prediction I think the Patriots will make some adjustments from last week and come out stronger in Week 10. New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will not have a valuable weapon when the team takes on the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday. On Saturday, the Patriots announced that they have placed running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve. This comes one week after Henderson announced he had experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency." On October 29, the Patriots placed Henderson on the injury report with an illness designation. He has not practiced since. "Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days," Henderson wrote in a statement on November 6. "During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable." After Henderson released his statement, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the franchise will do everything it can to support him. TreVeyon Henderson Was a Top Rookie Player Last Year "I know that he is well-loved and respected on this football team," Vrabel said last Friday, per NFL.com. " I'll support him, the best way that I know how is just to care for him, listen to him, and do whatever we can to get [him] healthy and get back, and to help this football team and to do what he loves." Henderson is in his second season with the Patriots. Last year, the 24-year-old finished third in Rookie of the Year voting after rushing for 911 yards and nine touchdowns. Henderson also caught 35 passes for 221 yards and one touchdown. This year, Henderson played in six games and rushed for 203 yards and one touchdown on 52 carries. His best game was against the Pittsburgh Steelers on September 20, when he posted 76 rushing yards and a touchdown. The Patriots are currently 5-4 and second place in the AFC East. away.blurb: A.J. Brown returned to practice for the first time in two weeks on Wednesday, Nov. 11 and has received an injury designation of "questionable" for Week 10. The designation is an indication that Brown could play in the game despite only practicing in a limited capacity all week. In Week 1, the former Eagle suffered a high ankle sprain and missed four games. Brown returned for two more games despite limited participation in practice. In Week 8, a knee injury was added to his status on New England's injury report, and he missed five more practices and two more games before his Nov. 11 return. Brown has now practiced three straight days – albeit in a limited capacity – and traveled with the Patriots to Munich. Brown is questionable to play in the Patriots' Week 10 game against the Lions . This week is the first that Brown has a status other than "out" since Week 7. The star receiver has missed New England's last two games while dealing with injuries to his ankle and knee. The Patriots' official website reported that Brown traveled to Germany with the team ahead of their matchup with the Lions in Munich. According to the team's injury report, he was a limited participant with ankle and knee injuries in all three days of practice leading up to Sunday's game on Nov. 15. Brown has not played since Oct. 22 against the Chicago Bears, while Stevenson got banged up last week in the blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers. Brown, who has missed six games out of nine possible in his inaugural season with the Patriots, wasn’t ruled out when the team announced offensive lineman Ben Brown (knee), cornerback Carlton Davis (knee), and RB Treveyon Henderson (illness) were inactive for Sunday before they traveled overseas. Brown made the long flight to Germany and was limited in practice all week, a sign he could make his second long-awaited return from his latest ailment. Head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Friday he felt “pretty good” about Brown’s chances of suiting up for Week 10 despite his questionable tag. It’s good news for Stevenson, whose injury didn’t look great and was quickly ruled out after going to the locker room during the Packers matchup. In addition to Brown and Stevenson being questionable, here are the seven others: FB Reggie Gilliam (knee) – designated for return from injured reserve OL Greg Van Roten (hamstring) – designated for return from IR As the Patriots’ offensive line woes continue with Ben Brown being ruled out, Vrabel told reporters on Friday he doesn’t know who will start at left guard. RB TreVeyon Henderson was ruled out for Week 10 and did not travel with the team as he recovers from a neurological medical emergency. He hasn’t played since Oct. 22 and has no timeline for return, but Vrabel offered some insight on the player’s situation. “I talk to TreVeyon every day and just like everybody else that’s not available, he’s working hard to get back and when that is, I don’t know,” Vrabel said (via MassLive ’s Mark Daniels). “I don’t have a timetable. home.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
home.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." KC is looking to build on its blowout win over the Jets in its previous outing. The Falcons have lost four of their past five matchups but aren't technically out of it given the dire state of the NFC South. As a result, Kevin Stefanski's group is viewing this contest as a must-win if they want to stay in the playoff race. Despite Kansas City's impressive 6-2 record, Andy Reid and Co. have dealt with special teams struggles and offensive inconsistencies. Those issues have put a damper on what has otherwise been a successful start. Most analysts view the Chiefs as heavy favorites, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor forecast? Chiefs on SI's Take Chiefs fans can only take things one week at a time. Until the Broncos lose and give Kansas City an opening, all the Chiefs can do is beat the opponents in front of them. The biggest storyline of this road clash is the arrival of Josh Downs , who landed with the Chiefs shortly before the trade deadline passed. The shifty slot receiver may not be featured too much out of the gate due to his unfamiliarity with the playbook, but there are bound to be some bright spots in his debut in the red and gold. Kenneth Walker III is a dynamic weapon in the backfield , but Bijan Robinson is on another level. In spite of poor quarterback play, Robinson is virtually unstoppable in the open field and possesses elite vision as a runner. He has three games in which he surpassed 100 yards this season and is averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Atlanta is unsurprisingly a significant underdog coming into this one, though it really depends on which version of the Falcons show up on Sunday. They were blown out by the Bengals last time out and shut out by the Buccaneers a week prior, but they also hold upset victories over the 49ers and Packers. The drastic shifts in Atlanta's play have fans scratching their heads, largely due to the play of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. A week after taking home NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors in Week 7, he tossed a career-high four interceptions and failed to get his team a point. Heading into their final game before a bye, the Falcons are going to throw everything they can at the visiting squad to stay in contention. This is the type of matchup that could see the Chiefs fall into an early deficit if they aren't careful. Nope, it wasn't Harrison Butker getting benched or cut. The switch was from the Falcons, who released kicker Nick Folk earlier this week and signed Jake Moody off the Ravens' practice squad. Chiefs fans may recall that Moody briefly held a record when he made a 55-yard field goal for the 49ers in Super Bowl LVIII, but Butker nailed a 57-yard attempt in the next quarter. That remains the longest field goal in Super Bowl history. Will kicking be a factor in Sunday's game? Could Moody give Atlanta a, ahem, leg up on the Chiefs? Here is how 67 national experts see things playing out in Sunday's game, which starts at noon and will be broadcast on KCTV (Ch. 5). This is from his story: "The Falcons pulled off a stunner against San Francisco three weeks ago but that was their Super Bowl." picks.blurb: Falcons Roundtable: Jessie Bates Trade, Ian Cunningham's Deadline and Chiefs Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football live updates Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved RAF Abu Dhabi: Chimaev crushes NFL news, live updates (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Christian Rauh · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 13, 2026 at 6:59 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Atlanta Falcons are looking to get back in the win column and keep their postseason hopes alive after losing their international game this past week against the Cincinnati Bengals. They now turn their attention to the Kansas City Chiefs, following a busy trade deadline for the Falcons new front office. On this week's Falcons Roundtable, the staff discusses the trades made at the deadline and how important this week's game is to getting back in the playoff picture. Following Atlanta's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati, what is your biggest concern about the Falcons? Michael Brauner: How much time do you have? The defense is not what we thought it was and Jessie Bates is now gone, the offense can't seem to find its identity and Michael Penix may not be the guy. It could get ugly the rest of the way if nothing changes. Christian Rauh: We've seen flashes of what Atlanta can accomplish, but they haven't been able to put together a complete performance. At some point, the Falcons have to stop making the same mistakes every week. Was trading Jessie Bates III the right decision, or should Atlanta have kept him? Michael Brauner: At the end of the day, as much as it stinks, this was absolutely the right decision. Getting legitimate draft capital in return for a safety who is getting older and on an expiring contract is always the right move, even if it hurts now. Christian Rauh: I don't love the decision to move on from Bates, but I understand it. The Falcons clearly have their eyes on the future, and getting draft capital back makes sense. However, replacing a player of his caliber isn't going to be easy, especially for a defense that already has plenty of questions. They did get some great value for him, though. What grade would you give Ian Cunningham for his first trade deadline with the Falcons? Michael Brauner: B+. There weren't many moves to be made, buying was out of the question, and they got real value for the guys they traded. Christian Rauh: B. It's clear he understands where this franchise currently stands and isn't afraid to make difficult decisions. Moving established starters isn't always popular, but Atlanta needs to build for the future. What must the Falcons do defensively to slow down Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on Sunday? Michael Brauner: This is not the same Chiefs offense from years ago. This is a unit who wants to run the ball and impose their will. Slow down Kenneth Walker, something few have done to this point, means slowing down this offense. Christian Rauh: It starts with getting pressure on Mahomes without allowing him to extend plays. Atlanta can't afford to give him time to sit in the pocket and pick apart the secondary. Is Sunday's game against Kansas City a must-win for Atlanta's playoff hopes, and who wins? Michael Brauner: .It is as must win as must win gets. Going into the bye week at 3-7 and losing three straight is pretty much season over. The NFC South is bad enough that perhaps they would still be alive, but on the brink. It's tough to have faith right now. Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Christian Rauh: Absolutely. At 3-6, the Falcons don't have much room for error if they want to remain in the playoff conversation. Unfortunately, I haven't seen enough consistency from Atlanta to believe they can knock off Kansas City. Chiefs 31, Falcons 17

away.headline: Kenneth Walker Injured, Latest Rumors on Chiefs RB vs. Falcons and Emmett Johnson Fantasy Outlook
away.blurb: Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chiefs are going to hold Walker out of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury because they "want to give him a week" rather than try to force him to play through it. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . After being a late addition to the injury report on Friday, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III won't play in Week 10. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added the injury is considered "minor" and the Chiefs want to exercise caution with Walker. From a fantasy perspective, Emmett Johnson should be a late addition to your roster on the waiver wire as he gets set to make his first career start. He is only rostered in 33 percent of leagues right now, per FantasyPros . Johnson was arguably the best player on the field for the Chiefs two weeks ago in their 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. He had 128 receiving yards and one touchdown on five receptions, as well as one carry for 15 yards in just 13 offensive snaps. Even though Atlanta's defense has been strong against the run, ranking third in EPA per rush, the ability Johnson showed as a receiver significantly boosts his fantasy value. away.headline: Chiefs rule out Kenneth Walker, NFL's No. 2 rusher, for Sunday's game in Atlanta with a groin injury
away.blurb: KANSAS CITY, Mo. (AP) — The Chiefs have ruled Kenneth Walker out of Sunday's game in Atlanta because of a groin injury, leaving them with rookie running back Emmett Johnson, ailing youngster Jaydn Ott and journeyman Nate Carter against Bijan Robinson and the Falcons. The Chiefs made the announcement Saturday, one day after listing Walker as questionable on their injury report. He had tweaked his groin in practice on Thursday, and coach Andy Reid said the team would be monitoring his progress over the next couple of days. Johnson has played well when given a chance this season, though. The overlooked fifth-round pick out of Nebraska has run 26 times for 111 yards and a touchdown, and he's caught 14 passes for 237 yards and another score. The bigger problem for the Chiefs is the lack of options behind Johnson on the depth chart. Brashard Smith went on injured reserve with a hamstring injury on Oct. 24, and Ott — who carried three times for 19 yards in mop-up duty in last week's blowout of the Jets — has been dealing with a sore hamstring of his own, leaving him questionable for Sunday's game in Atlanta. The Chiefs were flying to Atlanta on Saturday, and they did not expect any changes to their flight plan following the Federal Aviation Administration’s ground stoppage a day earlier. Defensive tackle Chris Jones was not traveling with the team for personal reasons, but the Chiefs said he would join the team in Atlanta and he carried no game designation. Walker is the league's second-leading rusher with 872 yards, trailing Robinson by just eight, though he's also played one fewer game than his Falcons counterpart. Walker also has caught 22 passes for 172 yards and four touchdowns. “He’s going to play anyway, whether Ken’s there or not,” Reid said Friday. “Everybody has confidence in him.” The Chiefs elevated Carter and wide receiver Jacob De Jesus from the practice squad Saturday. Carter spent last season with Atlanta, appearing in seven games and carrying nine times for 60 yards. He was waived by the Falcons as part of their final roster cuts, and Kansas City signed him to its practice squad a couple days later. See AP’s full NFL coverage here

They'll be taking the road trying to climb one game closer to .500, face up against another AFC Wild Card contender, and will be trying to build upon the 44-point outing they saw last weekend against the LA Chargers. So what can we expect from the Texans in this game against the Browns? Will they rise to the occasion for a second straight win, or fall into similar pitfalls that they have in their five losses so far this season? If the Texans can keep their momentum through the air and the offense can continue to limit the penalties setting them back as they did last weekend, 30 points is wildly possible for this team. Currently sitting at 3-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways long-term if they plan on making a postseason push in the AFC. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The good news? Sunday's matchup is on the road, a place where Houston is 3-1. The Texans will travel to Cleveland for a date with Deshaun Watson and the Browns in Week 10. Cleveland, which could be gunning for a wild-card berth under first-year coach Todd Monken, fell short on Sunday in a battle down in the bayou amid an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . Cleveland plans to start Watson, Houston's former franchise quarterback, but second-year passer Shedeur Sanders proved his potential by keeping the Browns alive in the Superdome. While throwing for nearly 200 yards and two touchdowns, Sanders was also sacked five times. Meanwhile, Cleveland's defense recorded five sacks, headlined by former Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger. "They're really good players, they're athletic and they're disruptive," Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley said. "They've got that speed off the ball. They use their hands and they play really hard continuously. They're a handful for sure." As for Houston, quarterback C.J. Stroud threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as Houston rolled past the Bolts in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. The Texans could be dealing with a multitude of injuries following Friday's practice. For the third straight day, rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge did not practice. Running back Woody Marks and defensive ends Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter also could be in trouble after missing practice on Thursday and Friday. away.headline: Browns place ex-Chiefs FB on IR ahead of Week 10 matchup vs. Texans
away.blurb: Former Kansas City Chiefs fullback Michael Burton was placed on the Cleveland Browns ' injured reserve list on November 14 ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup against the Houston Texans . Burton was a member of the Chiefs' Super Bowl LVII roster and originally entered the league as a fifth-round pick by the Detroit Lions in the 2015 NFL Draft. The veteran fullback has enjoyed a long and fruitful career, playing for seven teams over the course of his 11 years in the NFL. Cleveland announced its decision to place Burton on injured reserve in a post to the Browns' official Twitter account: Though Burton was never a superstar during his two-season tenure in Kansas City, he still managed to tally 33 yards on 13 attempts in 33 games with the Chiefs, and even managed to score one rushing touchdown. He also recorded five receptions for 42 yards in Andy Reid's offense. This article originally appeared on Chiefs Wire: Browns place ex-Chiefs FB on IR ahead of Week 10 matchup vs. Texans

Montgomery's case is simple: he's been dealing with a groin injury dating back to Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, has been out for the past three games, but was a full practice participant on Friday, that gives him hope to finally get back on the field for Week 10. home.headline: Texans' brutal injury report just gave the Browns a golden opportunity
home.blurb: The Browns will host a banged-up Texans team that has already ruled out edge rusher Danielle Hunter, linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., and left guard Keylan Rutledge. Will Anderson, Houston’s superstar pass rusher, also left Thursday’s practice with an ankle injury, was a nonparticipant on Friday, and is listed as questionable along with starting right tackle Trent Brown (wrist). Cleveland, meanwhile, has no major injury concerns. Top wide receiver Denzel Boston was listed as questionable with a toe injury , but the rookie practiced on Friday and is trending toward playing. The only Browns starter ruled out for Sunday is safety Ronnie Hickman with a concussion, but the Browns are deep at that position; second-round rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is slated to start Sunday’s game alongside veteran Grant Delpit. There could be openings in the middle of the field for head coach Todd Monken to exploit with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. and shifty wideout KC Concepcion. To'oTo'o is a solid linebacker for the Texans, but he’s been in and out of the lineup due to injuries himself this season and has struggled in pass coverage. The Browns felt like legitimate 4.5-point home underdogs for this game, especially after Houston demolished the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 9. But if Anderson joins the Texans’ inactives list on Sunday, the Browns could find themselves in prime position to pull off another upset. Texans could be missing exactly what they needed to exploit the Browns' biggest weakness The Texans were shaping up to be an extremely tough matchup for Cleveland, and they probably still are. But their defense potentially being down its top two pass rushers, along with Al-Shaair on the second level, changes everything. Anderson enters Week 10 as the NFL leader in sacks with 9.5. As a team, Houston moved into a tie for first place with the Minnesota Vikings last week. No quarterback, meanwhile, has been sacked more than Deshaun Watson, who’s been taken down 33 times in eight games. Keeping Watson upright will be one of the keys to this game regardless of who’s rushing off the edges. The Texans are one of the few teams in the NFL who have a worse rushing attack than the Browns — Houston is 29th, Cleveland is 25th — and it would behoove the Browns to play this game from ahead and force quarterback C.J. Stroud to throw from the pocket against Denzel Ward and their elite secondary. Al-Shaair’s absence is also pivotal. Without him, the Texans could have to move Henry To'oTo'o to middle linebacker or lean on a part-time player like Wade Woodaz for Sunday's game. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Pittsburgh always seems to be right in the thick of it in these division games, and the first matchup was decided by only three points. I think the scoring margin is the same here, but with slightly lower scoring, in keeping with the trend of divisional rematches. … Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 20 Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) (MNF) Dajani ( Chargers +4.5): This is potentially the worst Monday night game of all time. A winless team that hasn't covered the spread since last year vs. a spiraling team starting a new quarterback. Jacoby Brissett is an upgrade over Joe Fagnano , but how much of an upgrade immediately? I don't have a great read on this matchup, but I'll take Jim Harbaugh to keep things close with his brother's old team. … Prediction: Ravens 20, Chargers 17 Dubin (Chargers +4.5): I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. … Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20 Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Da

It’s a critical game for both teams. The Packers remain in last place in the NFC North, even while winning five of their last six games. The Vikings have lost two consecutive games following a 6-0 start. Who will win the game? And, with this being the halfway point of the season, who will lead the team in rushing, receiving and sacks? And, ultimately, what will be the team’s final record and playoff fate? Here are our Packers-Vikings picks and midseason predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Vikings Prediction The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins this week. It’s a huge move for the Vikings, who somehow are 6-2 despite their quarterbacks’ inability to get the ball to Justin Jefferson. Cousins has faced the Packers 10 times while with the Vikings. He topped a 110 passer rating in seven of those games. OK, but what about this season? With the Raiders, Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards, second in touchdown passes and 11th in passer rating. Plain and simple, he remains a quality starting quarterback. Maybe I’m guilty of overvaluing Cousins. Maybe I’m undervaluing Jordan Love’s ability to consistently make plays against a Vikings defense that has won every matchup this season. Ultimately, I think Cousins will make one more big play, Love will be forced into one more big mistake and the special teams will get in the way. Score: Vikings 20, Packers 17 Bill’s Record: 7-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Vikings Prediction Yes, Kirk Cousins is back, but Green Bay's defense is for real until proven otherwise. The Packers had some answers for Brian Flores' group in Week 1 until Jordan Love was snowed under by Minnesota's pressure. This time, Lambeau Field will be the X-factor as the offensive line will be able to hear Love manipulate the line of scrimmage, which will help him make one more play than Cousins, as the Packers score a big win heading into their bye week. Score: Packers 21, Vikings 17. Jacob’s Record: 6-3. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) waits for the snap against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? Bill: 11-6 (Losses at home to the Vikings and Bills and at the Bears). Jacob: 12-5 (Losses at home against Buffalo and at Chicago). Where Will Packers Finish in NFC North? Bill: Last (with the same record as the Vikings but by losing the tiebreaker). Jacob: Second (Chicago wins the NFC North thanks to a win on Christmas Day at Soldier Field). Who Will Lead Packers in Sacks? Bill: Lukas Van Ness. I came up with this question in light of Micah Parsons’ presumptive return for the game against the Rams. Tucker Kraft has had a quiet season following last year’s torn ACL. It’s just part of coming off a major injury. So, while I thought about going with Parsons here, Van Ness will maintain the team lead and finish with eight sacks. Jacob: Lukas Van Ness. Van Ness has 4.5 sacks, which leads the team. His job should get a little easier with Micah Parsons' return to the lineup as he'll see less double teams. Parsons is a good bet here, as well, but has noted it may take him a while to look like himself again. The goal for the Packers is going to be to have him at his best in the postseason. Who Will Lead Packers in Rushing? Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) rushes the ball against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Jacob: Kaleb Johnson leads the team in rushing, which is incredible considering how his season has gone to date. The guess here is that he's out of Matt LaFleur's doghouse and going to be a more focal point of Green Bay's offense in Josh Jacobs' absence. That will continue even when Jacobs returns to the lineup. Who Will Lead Packers in Receiving Yards? Bill: Christian Watson has 879 receiving yards, putting him on pace to blow past 1,650 yards. Matthew Golden has 783 receiving yards, putting him on pace to push for 1,500 yards. I’ll take Golden to surge to the lead, though. He has five consecutive games of six-plus catches and four consecutive games with 10-plus targets. The sheer volume of passes going to Golden will push him past the explosive play off Watson, especially if last week’s game signals that his drops are behind him. The big question: Can they set the combined yardage record? Jacob: Christian Watson. This might be one of the most intriguing storylines down the stretch. Watson and Golden are neck and neck in this category now, with Watson holding a slight advantage. Watson is used to playing this late in the season and has made some big plays in big games. Golden has, as well, so this will be really close as the season comes to a close, but give us Watson to go over 1,200 yards for the season and earn the team's receiving title. Will Jordan Love Lead NFL in Passing Yards? Bill: Entering Sunday, Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow leads the NFL with 298.3 passing yards per game. Jordan Love is hot on his heels with a 290.9-yard average. That’s less than a first down per game. Playing five consecutive cold-weather games down the stretch isn’t going to help Love in his pursuit. Jacob: Yes, the only way the Packers can move the ball is on the right arm of Jordan Love. There's little reason to believe that's going to change, even when the elements start turning colder. Add in some games that could be potential shootouts, like a home game against Buffalo or a road game against Chicago. That could cause Love to pile up some big numbers. How Will the Season End? Bill: With the entire NFC North earning their way into the playoff field, the last-place Packers will squeak into the postseason as the No. 7 seed. It’s obviously a familiar place for the Packers. And it’s a death sentence. The No. 7 seed has to play at the No. 2 seed. If the No. 7 pulls off an upset, it will have to play at the No. 1 seed. So, let’s roll with the Packers upsetting the rival Bears in the wild-card round but meeting their maker against the playoff-rival 49ers in the divisional round. Jacob: The Packers will earn the NFC's fifth seed and have a date with the NFC South-winning Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first round of the playoffs. A big game from Jordan Love and Christian Watson, coupled with a suffocating defensive performance in which Micah Parsons will collect three sacks and a forced fumble against Baker Mayfield, will give the team its first playoff win since 2023. They will follow that by avenging last year's loss in the playoffs to the Chicago Bears by knocking them out at Soldier Field in the divisional round on a game-winning field goal from Trey Smack. That sends them to San Francisco, a house of horrors, for the NFC Championship Game, where the season ultimately will end with Brock Purdy leading a late touchdown drive to send the Packers into an offseason short of the Super Bowl. No team has ever blitzed as much as this year's Vikings, and they have blitzed Packers QB Jordan Love with even greater frequency. Vikings fans are still riding the excitement from a major adrenaline injection early this week as the team reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins via trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. What once looked like a potential beatdown in Green Bay now looks like a massive opportunity for the Vikings to end a two-game losing streak and sweep their biggest rival. There’s still a lot up in the air, especially since head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn't technically named Cousins the starter yet. But let’s be real: Cousins is starting unless there's a major setback . So, let’s dive into some predictions for Sunday, assuming “Kirko Chainz” makes his triumphant return. 1. Justin Jefferson returns to form (for real this time) Frick it, Justin Jefferson is down there somewhere. There is perhaps no larger beneficiary of the Cousins’ reunion tour than Jefferson. The seventh-year wide receiver is on pace to have the worst year of his career after poor QB play wrecked his 2025 campaign. Needless to say, it’s time for Jefferson to reclaim his spot on the wide receiver throne. away.headline: Packers appear built to withstand key injuries vs. Vikings in Week 10
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers are set to face the Minnesota Vikings in a game they must win to remain in the thick of the NFC North race . At 6-3, the Packers could move ahead of Minnesota in the division rankings if they come out on top. The Packers listed Xavier McKinney and Kevin Zeitler as questionable The Packers posted their final injury report for Week 10. Offensive guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps), safety Xavier McKinney (foot), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (back), Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), and running back Chris Moore (ankle) had the questionable designation. Now, just because they popped up on the injury report doesn't mean that they won't be available against the Vikings. That said, not having McKinney would be a huge blow. If the All-Pro safety isn't good to go, Kitan Oladapo may get the starting nod next to Evan Williams. However, the task became substantially tougher when the Vikes traded for Kirk Cousins. Compounding the issue is that Green Bay could be without a handful of key players. Oladapo logged 14 defensive snaps in the win over the New England Patriots when Evan Williams briefly left the bout . He has played a total of 28 snaps at safety that year, so you can bet Kirk Cousins could try to target him. The silver lining is that defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has done a good job of game-planning for Kirk throughout his coaching career , so he should have a trick or two prepared to stop the Minnesota offense. On the other hand, Green Bay should be able to withstand Zeitler's absence if he isn't good to go. If the veteran hog molly doesn't suit up, the Packers can easily plug in Laken Tomlinson at right guard and Aaron Banks on the left side. Granted, that's the lineup they've employed the past two games. Then again, the expectation was that after Zeitler made his debut against New England, he would see an uptick in playing time and possibly start at right guard. However, it looks like the coaching staff will have to halt the plan, as injuries have prevented him from hitting his stride since landing in Titletown in late September. Jordan Love gives the Packers the best chance to beat the VIkings Whether Kevin Zeitler starts or not, the Green Bay offensive line will be in good shape in Week 10. And that's the thing, if the Packers want to have a shot at beating Minnesota, they will need to keep Jordan Love upright. The Vikes have the top-ranked defense in the NFL. Sure, their run defense is 22nd in yards allowed, but can you truly trust Green Bay's underwhelming rushing attack to move the football? That means that it will be up to Love to put the team on his shoulders, and having a clean pocket will most definitely help. If defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon and his unit, with or without Xavier McKinney, can generate enough stops and give the offense a couple extra possessions, the Packers should be able to earn their seventh win of the season. The eighth-year quarterback has just 1,022 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. Wentz struggled mightily when he stepped in for Murray on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. He completed just 32 percent of his passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions. Minnesota showed interest in reuniting with Cousins prior to Monday night , but Wentz' poor performance likely made it easier for the Vikings to name Cousins as the starter for a pivotal matchup against the Green Bay Packers in Week 10. Cousins is already familiar with head coach Kevin O'Connell's offensive system from the last two seasons of his six-year stint in Minnesota. He also has plenty of chemistry with star wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who enjoyed his most productive years on the receiving end of Cousins' passes. Cousins and O'Connell both struggled after parting ways, but they now have an opportunity to make up for lost time. Still, Murray's availability could prove valuable behind a 38-year-old quarterback. Until then, the backup role will go to Wentz, and second-year quarterback Max Brosmer will serve as the emergency No. 3 option. 12:57 Week 10 RB Rankings 📊 TOP NEWS Jefferson Reacts to Cousins Trade Bleacher Report • 4h Georgia Commit Dies at 18 Bleacher Report • 3h Josh Hart 'Not In a Good Head Space' Bleacher Report • 8h NFL to Address Trade 'Snafus' Bleacher Report • 5h Jeremiah Breaks 4th B1G Record 🚨 Bleacher Report • 6h USA Crushes Haiti 6-0 in 1st Leg Bleacher Report • 14h 1 Word to Describe Knicks 💬 Bleacher Report • 6h Data revealed on robot umpire's impact to MLB ejections Bleacher Report • 12h Titans Unveil 'Music City' Unis 🎵 Bleacher Report • 14h Unpopular Trade Ideas 💡

home.headline: Packers appear built to withstand key injuries vs. Vikings in Week 10
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers are set to face the Minnesota Vikings in a game they must win to remain in the thick of the NFC North race . At 6-3, the Packers could move ahead of Minnesota in the division rankings if they come out on top. The Packers listed Xavier McKinney and Kevin Zeitler as questionable The Packers posted their final injury report for Week 10. Offensive guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps), safety Xavier McKinney (foot), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (back), Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), and running back Chris Moore (ankle) had the questionable designation. Now, just because they popped up on the injury report doesn't mean that they won't be available against the Vikings. That said, not having McKinney would be a huge blow. If the All-Pro safety isn't good to go, Kitan Oladapo may get the starting nod next to Evan Williams. However, the task became substantially tougher when the Vikes traded for Kirk Cousins. Compounding the issue is that Green Bay could be without a handful of key players. Oladapo logged 14 defensive snaps in the win over the New England Patriots when Evan Williams briefly left the bout . He has played a total of 28 snaps at safety that year, so you can bet Kirk Cousins could try to target him. The silver lining is that defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has done a good job of game-planning for Kirk throughout his coaching career , so he should have a trick or two prepared to stop the Minnesota offense. On the other hand, Green Bay should be able to withstand Zeitler's absence if he isn't good to go. If the veteran hog molly doesn't suit up, the Packers can easily plug in Laken Tomlinson at right guard and Aaron Banks on the left side. Granted, that's the lineup they've employed the past two games. Then again, the expectation was that after Zeitler made his debut against New England, he would see an uptick in playing time and possibly start at right guard. However, it looks like the coaching staff will have to halt the plan, as injuries have prevented him from hitting his stride since landing in Titletown in late September. Jordan Love gives the Packers the best chance to beat the VIkings Whether Kevin Zeitler starts or not, the Green Bay offensive line will be in good shape in Week 10. And that's the thing, if the Packers want to have a shot at beating Minnesota, they will need to keep Jordan Love upright. The Vikes have the top-ranked defense in the NFL. Sure, their run defense is 22nd in yards allowed, but can you truly trust Green Bay's underwhelming rushing attack to move the football? That means that it will be up to Love to put the team on his shoulders, and having a clean pocket will most definitely help. If defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon and his unit, with or without Xavier McKinney, can generate enough stops and give the offense a couple extra possessions, the Packers should be able to earn their seventh win of the season. home.headline: NFL insider reveals Josh Jacobs injury return timeline for Packers after surgery
home.blurb: Green Bay Packers star running back Josh Jacobs suffered a fractured ring finger on his right hand during his team’s 45-27 beatdown of the New England Patriots this past weekend, leaving his availability in question. The injury required surgery, and now an update has emerged on Jacobs’ potential return for the Packers. According to Netflix NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Jacobs underwent successful surgery on his fractured ring finger on Friday in Los Angeles, with noted hand and wrist surgeon Dr. Steven Shin performing the procedure. Pelissero reported that Jacobs is expected to return to the Packers in the “next several weeks.” What George Pickens’ Bizarre Answer Means for His Cowboys Return vs. 49ers That could bode well for a Packers team that has won its last two games to improve to 6-3 this season in the competitive NFC North. Jacobs missed six games after being placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List amid a domestic dispute and the NFL reinstated Jacobs last month. However, his three games since returning haven’t been as productive as he or the team may have hoped. Jacobs recorded 36 carries for just 80 yards and one touchdown before suffering his finger injury against New England. More news: Lions HC Dan Campbell Reveals Major Drake Maye Concern Before Patriots Clash He’s been a key offensive component for the Packers for the past two seasons. He had 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns in his debut season for Green Bay, and then 929 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns last season. With Jacobs sidelined for the next several weeks, Kaleb Johnson could now take on a bigger workload for the Packers. Johnson has appeared in seven games, tallying 42 carries for 172 yards and one touchdown. MarShawn Lloyd has played in eight games for the Packers and has 149 rushing yards with two touchdowns to give Green Bay additional options at the position. Green Bay is heading into a challenging matchup this Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings, considered one of the league’s top defenses. The Packers’ running game could be important in taking pressure off quarterback Jordan Love. The Vikings also just added quarterback Kirk Cousins ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, potentially providing a significant upgrade for a struggling offense in the competitive NFC North. The Green Bay Packers face the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 15, beginning at 1 p.m. ET. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday’s estimates. That doesn’t bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We’ll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10.
