Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. away.headline: Week 10 Super Bowl stock report: Jaguars go all-in at trade deadline, injuries ravage Patriots offense
away.blurb: User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl race coming out of the trade deadline and heading into Week 10. These newcomers join a team that already holds a three-game lead in its division. They will also line up on the other side of the ball from an offense that is cooking with gas. The fourth-highest-scoring unit in the NFL has flat-out demolished half of its opponents. Trevor Lawrence , somehow, is still somewhat flying under the radar — probably because his offense keeps building such large leads that he does not need to rack up passing numbers in the second halves of these blowouts. Parker Washington has turned into a star, and Bhayshul Tuten emerged as a bona fide No. 1 running back. All of the pieces are in place. Just when it seemed like the Patriots were starting to put everything back together, they hit another rough patch. Just like they did to open the season, they have lost two of their last three games. The only win in that stretch was a five-point squeaker against the lowly Miami Dolphins . The road ahead does not get a whole lot easier with five likely playoff teams on the schedule over the next eight weeks. It is going to be a battle to return to the postseason after last year's run to the Super Bowl. Don't look now, but the Houston Texans are not out of it yet. The AFC South will remain out of reach so long as the Jaguars do not shockingly collapse, so it is Wild Card or bust for a squad that started the year at 0-4. At just 1.5 games back, the Texans are right in the mix. Since that winless first month of the season, the Texans have won three of four and took two of those games in blowout fashion. They just put up a season-high 44 points on the bottom-dwelling Los Angeles Chargers in a game that emphasized how far C.J. Stroud has come as a quarterback. He continues to play the best football of his career and is not even remotely the reason why the Texans are still two games under .500. Tank Dell's return to the wide receiver group and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s addition about a month ago also gave him a deep stable of pass-catchers to target, and he is cashing in. Losses are rare in the NFC North. At least one team has to add one to their tally in Week 10, though. The Packers are the only team with three losses, so every matchup means a little bit more to them as they try to work their way out of the shallow basement of the NFL's best division — one that could send all four teams to the postseason . They will have vengeance on their minds on Sunday as they seek to get payback for what the Minnesota Vikings did to them in a stunning second-half comeback in Week 1. But they will have to do so against a Vikings offense that should be far better the rest of the season now that Kirk Cousins is in at quarterback. Week 10 injury report:

Tuten played in last week's game against the Baltimore Ravens despite not practicing that week with a foot/ankle injury, and he also sat out the first two practice days this week. He ended up getting 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown a week ago and did participate in Friday's practice as a limited participant, giving him the green light for Sunday against the Titans. The Jaguars had their third-worst rushing performance in terms of EPA/Rush during the 25-game Coen era on Thursday Night Football. Part of this had to do with execution, while another part of it had to do with a run-heavy second-half script after the Jaguars got up on the Ravens at halftime. Add in some bad weather that took the ball out of the hands of the passing game, and the Jaguars' rushing attack had the perfect storm for a regression game. As Coen said, there should be no long-term concerns. But in an AFC where the race for the No. 1 seed will be important week in and week out, and the Jaguars will need their running game to continue hitting its stride over the second-half of the season. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Well, technically. The Colts, 2-7, could claim the top spot, but they do not own their own first-round for the next draft, with the New York Jets holding that selection as part of an in-season trade last year that sent cornerback Sauce Gardner to Indianapolis. Despite the Dolphins' positive signs of growth over the past several weeks, the oddsmakers have given the Colts a slight nod in this game. The FanDuel Sportsbook line opened with Indianapolis favored by 2.5 points , slightly under the typical three-point advantage given to a home team, and it has remained steady as of Tuesday morning. The point total is set at 40.5, while Miami is +116 on the money line for the straight-up win. The Colts are -136 for the win. This week could see massive changes in odds as Tuesday's trade deadline approaches. Indianapolis is expected to be sellers today, with running back Jonathan Taylor considered one of the top available players on the market, and rumors swirling around defensive tackle Grover Stewart and quarterback Daniel Jones. If the Colts do start making trades ahead of the 4 p.m. Eastern deadline, how will the line move? Miami could also be sellers, with teams reportedly interested in players like linebacker Jordyn Brooks and defensive tackle Zach Sieler. The Dolphins may not be eager to move on from core pieces of their rebuild, but they may be offered a package of draft picks they cannot refuse. Tuesday could significantly affect the odds for this weekend's game, but for now, the Colts are slightly favored.

away.headline: Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report
away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. Wright has been dealing with a quad injury that led to him being ruled out in Week 9. Now, he is set to return against the Colts. Brewer has now missed his second straight practice, as he is currently in concussion protoco l. It is not unlikely that he will suit up against the Indianapolis Colts. The full injury report is as follows: Running back Kaytron Allen (quad), safety Michael Taaffe (wrist), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and running back Jaylen Wright (quad) were all full participants yet again. Despite the semblance of a laundry list of injured players, the Dolphins look to be in decent shape. Losing Brewer will be a huge hit to the offense, but Andrew Meyer will be there to step in. Meyer spoke on Thursday about not only learning from "the best center in the league" but also stating that he has the confidence to step in for the Miami offensive line if that is what happens. The Dolphins are looking for their second win of the season, as they will face the struggling Colts. Indianapolis may not be a pushover opponent, but they also got rid of many players at the trade deadline, leaving this to be a potential "easier" matchup for Miami.

away.headline: Dolphins-Colts Game Preview and Predictions: Can Miami Overcome Injuries?
away.blurb: That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. Analysis: This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. For a change, the Miami Dolphins are given a chance by more than just one or two national media members heading into their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts — and that's despite the injury to starting quarterback Malik Willis. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. away.headline: Breaking Down the Dolphins Saturday Updates for the Indianapolis Game
away.blurb: Reagor being elevated would seem to indicate that wide receiver Chris Bell indeed will be inactive after being listed as doubtful on the final injury report of the week with a knee injury that kept him out of practice Thursday and Friday. Along with potentially getting snaps at wide receiver, Reagor also becomes an option to return punts and/or kickoffs. Bell will be joining Jalen Wayne, who was ruled out Friday, on the inactive list. Reagor will join Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas, Kevin Coleman Jr. and Jalen Tolbert on the game-day roster. Lastly, as expected, the Dolphins didn't activate cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. off PUP and officially was downgraded to out on the injury report. The Miami Dolphins made the expected moves Saturday ahead of their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts, but they still have an opening to be filled at some point. The Dolphins announced early Saturday afternoon they had signed kicker Zane Gonzalez to the 53-man roster off the practice squad, along with elevating quarterback Brady Cook and wide receiver Jalen Reagor. Head coach Jeff Hafley already had indicated earlier this week the team would be signing Gonzalez to the active roster, which was the only way he could kick again for Miami this season after exhausting his three allowed elevations. The move can be questioned based on Gonzalez missed a field goal each of the past two games, although special teams coordinator Chris Tabor said Thursday the miss against the New England in Week 8 was more about the whole operation than a Gonzalez mistake. "I think he's a good player," Tabor said. "I think he's a player that, yes, he missed a kick he should have made. We can all agree about that and Zane would too. In my eyes, that's kind of his first miss. I know on stats that it's two, sometimes there's other things that go on. I'm just not really, I'm not a guy that just pushes players away. He's been on the street for six weeks, seven weeks, and this was his third week back, so I think that he's still working to get to where he needs to be, right? I got a lot of confidence in him and we're working hard at getting better. I look forward to watching him kick this weekend. I got a lot of confidence in him, and it's real easy for me." The signing of Gonzalez put the Dolphins at 52 players on the active roster after the moves this week that saw QB Malik Willis and DT Zach Sieler go on injured reserve, CB Reese Taylor getting waived, and DT Keith Cooper Jr. signed off the Carolina Panthers practice squad. Cook was on the active roster earlier this season before being waived and re-signed to the practice squad, and he seemed like a logical choice to be re-signed to the 53 if he's going to back up new starter Kyle McCord for the next four games while Willis is on IR. Technically, the Dolphins don't have to make that decision until after Cook has been elevated three times, which woud come after the Week 12 game against the New York Jets. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. Analysis: This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. For a change, the Miami Dolphins are given a chance by more than just one or two national media members heading into their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts — and that's despite the injury to starting quarterback Malik Willis. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. home.blurb: Wide receiver Chris Bell has been limited in practice this week with a knee issue. Hafley said he would not practice on Friday and is doubtful, but he has not been ruled out. Hafley said Bell got hit in the leg during practice and it did not have to do with his prior knee injury. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

away.headline: Saints Injury Report: Tyler Shough Loses Two Key Protectors Against Panthers
away.blurb: Head coach Kellen Moore ruled out multiple players with injuries, including two starting offensive linemen: center Erik McCoy (bicep) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee). The team will also miss rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) and second-round defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee). The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. Moore said Fuaga isn’t expected to miss enough time to land on injured reserve, but McCoy’s outlook is less certain. A few other players are questionable for Sunday’s game with the Carolina Panthers. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is the big name, but cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is one to watch, too. We’ll find out for sure when the inactives list is published on Sunday. The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed in Sunday’s rivalry game with the Carolina Panthers , with the heaviest hits being on the offensive line. Saints Offensive Line Facing Major Adjustments The Saints got more than three quarters of action from their starting offensive line in last week's win over the Cleveland Browns before McCoy exited with a biceps injury. The situation worsened when Fuaga suffered a knee sprain during practice, leaving New Orleans without two important pieces of its offensive front. Moore indicated Fuaga's injury is not expected to require a stint on injured reserve, although McCoy's recovery timeline remains uncertain. McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center. Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard. Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup. The Saints also dealt with injuries involving left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and guard David Edwards (knee) throughout the week. While both returned to full participation Friday, it’s another sign that this unit is not even close to 100%. Even with Banks and Edwards, losing two starters makes it hard for an offensive line that has struggled with pass protection and consistency in the running game. away.headline: Report: Saints to activate Travis Etienne Jr. for Week 10 vs. Panthers
away.blurb: In his first three games to start 2026 in New Orleans, Etienne rushed for 128 yards and averaged 4.3 per carry. He also had 11 receptions for 51 yards. Etienne was having his best game as a Saint in Week 3 against the Raiders, rushing for 57 yards, before going down with a hamstring injury in the third quarter. He was placed on injured reserve the following week and has missed the last five games before returning to practice this week. By the end of the week, he was practicing in full capacity and was officially listed as questionable to face Carolina on the week's final injury report. As expected, the Ringer's Tom Pelissero reports the New Orleans Saints plan to activate running back Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve for their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The 3-5 Saints and Panthers play for sole possession of first place in the NFC South division. This will be the first action for Etienne since Week 3 back on Sept. 27 against the Raiders . Etienne, 27, was signed to a three-year contract by the Saints in free agency last offseason. He was expected to be the lead back for a New Orleans offense that ranked 28th in rushing production in 2025, the team's first year under head coach Kellen Moore. Etienne starred at Jennings High School in Louisiana before playing collegiately for the Clemson Tigers as a three-time All-American and twice ACC Offensive Player of the Year. A first round choice of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2021 NFL Draft, Etienne rushed for over 1,000 yards three times in four seasons between 2022 and 2025 before being signed by the Saints in free agency. Etienne is expected to share backfield duties with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara against the Panthers. Estime is coming off 72 rushing yards last week against the Browns, a season-high for any New Orleans runner. Kamara has 157 rushing yards and an average of 3.3 per carry over seven games this season. The Saints come into Week 10 ranked 26th in rushing with an average of 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 per carry. They'll face a Panthers defense ranked 28th against the run, giving up 4.6 per rush and an average of 133.4 yards per contest. away.headline: Struggling Panthers could get 5 starters, 4 reserves back from injuries in the coming weeks
away.blurb: Carolina opened the 21-day practice windows on Wednesday for cornerback Mike Jackson, wide receiver Xavier Legette and running back Jonathon Brooks to return from injured reserve. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, guard Damien Lewis and cornerback Will Lee III returned to practice after missing time with injuries, while versatile offensive lineman Brady Christensen entered his second week in the 21-day practice window and is nearing his return. Coach Dave Canales said it's too early in the week to know who'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Saints. The Panthers held a light practice on Wednesday, and Canales said he should know more later in the week once the medical staff is able to evaluate the injured players' progress. home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Tyler Shough Loses Two Key Protectors Against Panthers
home.blurb: Head coach Kellen Moore ruled out multiple players with injuries, including two starting offensive linemen: center Erik McCoy (bicep) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee). The team will also miss rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) and second-round defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee). The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. Moore said Fuaga isn’t expected to miss enough time to land on injured reserve, but McCoy’s outlook is less certain. A few other players are questionable for Sunday’s game with the Carolina Panthers. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is the big name, but cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is one to watch, too. We’ll find out for sure when the inactives list is published on Sunday. The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed in Sunday’s rivalry game with the Carolina Panthers , with the heaviest hits being on the offensive line. Saints Offensive Line Facing Major Adjustments The Saints got more than three quarters of action from their starting offensive line in last week's win over the Cleveland Browns before McCoy exited with a biceps injury. The situation worsened when Fuaga suffered a knee sprain during practice, leaving New Orleans without two important pieces of its offensive front. Moore indicated Fuaga's injury is not expected to require a stint on injured reserve, although McCoy's recovery timeline remains uncertain. McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center. Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard. Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup. The Saints also dealt with injuries involving left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and guard David Edwards (knee) throughout the week. While both returned to full participation Friday, it’s another sign that this unit is not even close to 100%. Even with Banks and Edwards, losing two starters makes it hard for an offensive line that has struggled with pass protection and consistency in the running game. home.headline: Report: Saints to activate Travis Etienne Jr. for Week 10 vs. Panthers
home.blurb: In his first three games to start 2026 in New Orleans, Etienne rushed for 128 yards and averaged 4.3 per carry. He also had 11 receptions for 51 yards. Etienne was having his best game as a Saint in Week 3 against the Raiders, rushing for 57 yards, before going down with a hamstring injury in the third quarter. He was placed on injured reserve the following week and has missed the last five games before returning to practice this week. By the end of the week, he was practicing in full capacity and was officially listed as questionable to face Carolina on the week's final injury report. As expected, the Ringer's Tom Pelissero reports the New Orleans Saints plan to activate running back Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve for their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The 3-5 Saints and Panthers play for sole possession of first place in the NFC South division. This will be the first action for Etienne since Week 3 back on Sept. 27 against the Raiders . Etienne, 27, was signed to a three-year contract by the Saints in free agency last offseason. He was expected to be the lead back for a New Orleans offense that ranked 28th in rushing production in 2025, the team's first year under head coach Kellen Moore. Etienne starred at Jennings High School in Louisiana before playing collegiately for the Clemson Tigers as a three-time All-American and twice ACC Offensive Player of the Year. A first round choice of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2021 NFL Draft, Etienne rushed for over 1,000 yards three times in four seasons between 2022 and 2025 before being signed by the Saints in free agency. Etienne is expected to share backfield duties with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara against the Panthers. Estime is coming off 72 rushing yards last week against the Browns, a season-high for any New Orleans runner. Kamara has 157 rushing yards and an average of 3.3 per carry over seven games this season. The Saints come into Week 10 ranked 26th in rushing with an average of 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 per carry. They'll face a Panthers defense ranked 28th against the run, giving up 4.6 per rush and an average of 133.4 yards per contest. home.headline: Saints roster moves: Second-round pick lands on injured reserve
home.blurb: Miller is a rookie second round pick, the 42nd overall selection, who was expected to fortify the middle of the Saints defense. Through eight games, Miller had only appeared in four contests and just 32% of the team's defensive snaps in those outings with 5 total tackles. Dealing with a knee injury, the Saints had already ruled Miller out on Fridays injury report before the decision to place him on injured reserve on Saturday. In advance of their Week 10 matchup against the Carolina Panthers , the New Orleans Saints announced a few roster moves on Saturday afternoon. Rookie defensive tackle Christen Miller has been placed on injured reserve. Kicker Charlie Smyth and offensive tackle Easton Kilty were elevated from the practice squad to the active roster, with Kilty being a standard elevation for the week. Running back Travis Etienne was officially activated from injured reserve. Etienne was the biggest move. He's missed the last five games with a hamstring injury but was signed to a three-year contract last offseason to be the Saints featured running back. Through the first three games, Etienne had 128 rushing yards and a 4.3 average with 11 receptions for 51 yards. Expect Etienne to share backfield reps fairly evenly with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara. Estime had 72 yards rushing in last week's win over Cleveland, a season-high for any New Orleans running back. Kilty's elevation makes sense. He can play multiple positions along the offensive line and the Saints will be without injured center Erik McCoy (biceps) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) this Sunday and for probably several weeks to follow. At least initially, right guard Cesar Ruiz will slide into McCoy's spot with either rookie fourth round choice Jeremiah Wright or William Sherman playing right guard. Fuaga will be replaced by either Asim Richards or rookie Mason Murphy. Smyth gets his second straight week at kicker as a replacement for the released Daniel Carlson. After Blake Grupe was released at mid-season last year, Smyth was 12 of 16 on field goal attempts through the last six games. He'd lose the job in training camp before being elevated from the practice squad last week to replace Carlson. New Orleans and Carolina both come into this game with 3-5 records and tied for first place in the NFC South. The winner of this Superdome showdown will take sole possession of first place. New Orleans swept Carolina last season and are 10-4 against the Panthers since 2019. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Saints roster moves: Second-round pick lands on injured reserve

The Buffalo Bills are in pole position for the AFC No. 1 seed, and a visit to the 2-7 New York Jets on Sunday isn't likely to slow down Josh Allen and Co. TOP PICK Bills vs Jets prediction: Over 50.5 It'll take more than a short week to impact a Buffalo Bills offense that leads the league with 386.4 yards per game and 32 points per game — and this AFC East showdown with the New York Jets provides a familiar punching bag, with Buffalo scoring 30+ points in four of the last five meetings . Behind Josh Allen and James Cook , the Bills are scoring on 67% of their red-zone trips — a rate they could improve against New York's shaky run defense. The Over has also cashed in three of Buffalo's four road games this year. But this pick is about the Jets, too. Garrett Wilson 's return will fuel the New York passing game, and Geno Smith won't shy away from throwing downfield — he's completed a pass of 40+ yards in four straight games. The Over is 3-1 in the hosts' past four contests , and I'd play this up to 56%. Bills vs Jets combo After giving up 73 points over the last two games, the Jets' defense is a gift to Over bettors, and Allen has a healthy receiving corps capable of producing big plays. Buckle up for a major mismatch when the potent Buffalo ground game ( 146.6 rushing yards per game , second in the NFL) collides with a New York run defense that allows 128 rushing yards per game, ranking in the bottom 10. That paves the way for Cook to pile up carries. He's gone over this rushing attempts line in four straight games , and the Bills could lean even more heavily on the run if they build a big lead. Look for Allen to benefit, too. With nine rushing TDs already this season, he's been unstoppable near the goal line. His scrambles to escape a dangerous Jets pass rush could also carry him into the end zone. James Cook Over 19.5 rushing attempts Josh Allen anytime TD Bills vs Jets touchdown scorer: Keon Coleman There are more mouths to feed in Buffalo's offense with DJ Moore healthy again. But neither Moore nor Khalil Shakir offers the same red-zone threat as Keon Coleman , who's hauled in three touchdown catches this year. Coleman has earned Allen's trust, drawing 15 targets in his last three games , and his 6-foot-3 frame makes him a natural target on jump balls and fades. With the Bills likely to find success on the ground against a struggling Jets defense, play-action shots downfield could also create anytime TD value for Coleman. I'd play this up to 30%. The Bills defeated the Jets 35-8. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Jets will be a home underdog against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, having lost seven of their last eight games. Other than a last-gasp loss to the Patriots in week four, the Bills' record is unblemished this year. Surely the Jets can't pull off an upset, can they? Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to flip their season on its head: It's a trap! America is already looking ahead to the Bills-Chiefs game scheduled to take place in the evening of Thanksgiving Thursday. While Buffalo has two games to play between now and then, they will feel good about their chances of still only having one loss after playing the Jets this week and Miami next week. Kansas City has lost just twice so this could be decisive in the race for the AFC's top seed. We've seen situations like this before though. While the Jets are rarely the team to take advantage of the opportunity, their profile as a team that has kept a lot of games close and come up just short in the end could make them dangerous if the Bills get complacent. And if they did get complacent, who could blame them? After all, the last time these teams met, the Bills rested all of their starters and still won 35-8. Then again, that was a very different Jets team too. The only current non-offensive line starters who started that game are Harrison Phillips, Jamien Sherwood and Adonai Mitchell. Can Mitchell bounce back? It's become traditional this year to have at least one high profile player that doesn't get the ball on offense. Last week, it was Adonai Mitchell, a player who seven days earlier, had posted the best numbers of his career. The Jets really seem to be struggling with the whole "many mouths to feed" aspect of having provided their quarterback with an adequate number of pass catching weapons for the first time in several seasons. However, Mitchell not seeing the ball last week was not for the want of trying as he was thrown to seven times. Opening drive success We could easily spend column inches here talking about why the Jets can't convert in the red zone, or how they shouldn't abandon the running game, or when are they ever going to intercept another pass, but how about we discuss something they have actually been doing well? For each of the past five games, the Jets have driven downfield and scored on their opening possession, which has played a big part in them still being competitive heading into the second half of each game. So, now we have to ask the question – can this continue? And…how will the team react if it doesn't? This isn't the first time in recent memory that the offensive has looked good early on in games, and executed the scripted part of the gameplan effectively, only to then go on to struggle in the second half when points are needed to convert wins. Back in 2020, where Adam Gase's Jets were in danger of going winless until very late in the season, they actually scored eight times in a row on their opening drive. The current decision makers would ideally not like to have too many similarities to that 2020 team. Gregory Rousseau's ascent to super-stardom The biggest threat on the Bills defense is obviously edge rusher Gregory Rousseau, who is having a monster year. After just eight games, Rousseau has already tied his career-high with eight sacks, while also doubling his career mark for passes defensed with another eight. Rousseau primarily lines up on the left, so it will be mostly up to Armand Membou to try and keep him quiet. Rousseau had a two sack game against the Jets in his second season in 2022, but surprisingly otherwise only has one sack in eight other games against the Jets. The Bills are 7-2 in these matchups, though. Having not been traded, is Will McDonald's role going to change? The Jets opted not to trade former first round pick Will McDonald during the week, despite reports of interest from a number of teams. Head coach Aaron Glenn has been suggesting McDonald is still very much in the Jets plans for the rest of this season, and he is of course under contract for next year after New York exercised his fifth year option. He even implied McDonald had earned a bigger role. McDonald's defensive snap count percentage has dropped from 66% in both 2024 and 2025 to just 46% in 2026 and, even more confoundingly, his percentage of run snaps has increased. Will an increase in playing time for McDonald happen on Sunday? And, if it does, are we destined to see diminishing returns in regard to his production? What's the plan for the secondary? A matchup against the team with the number one offense in the entire NFL is not really the ideal time to experiment with line-up changes but the Jets are desperately striving for more consistency from their back seven, in addition to having an undermanned front that is struggling to stop the run. Having missed a meeting and made some on-field mistakes, the previous starting slot corner – Jarvis Brownlee Jr. – is in the doghouse. However, rookie D'Angelo Ponds has looked overmatched at times which is hardly surprising given how he is learning a new position and missed half of training camp. New York also experimented with using Minkah Fitzpatrick in the slot on Sunday, elevating Malachi Moore into the lineup at safety for basically the first time all year. Could this be the answer? Time will tell. Let us know how you see things going in Sunday's game in the comments section…

away.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown was the only Bills player who did not practice Thursday because of an ankle injury. away.headline: Buffalo Bills Handed Concerning Injury News on $72M Starter
away.blurb: Buffalo Bills Handed Concerning Injury News on $72M Starter Unlock the latest Heavy on Bills news — direct to your inbox. The Buffalo Bills could be without an impact starter on Sunday against the New York Jets . Buffalo's offensive line has been hindered by injuries as of late. Starting right tackle Spencer Brown missed the game two weeks ago. Then, last week, starting left tackle Dion Dawkins and starting left guard Alec Anderson were inactive due to injuries. The Bills will now go on the road to play the Jets on Sunday. Buffalo Bills Get Concerning Injury News on Spencer Brown Bills get injury news on Spencer Brown. Buffalo got Brown back from injury last week but he once again could be inactive on Sunday. Brown is in the midst of a four-year, $72 million deal and is a key part of the offensive line. However, he's been on the injury report again, and The Athletic's Joe Buscagalia believes it's unlikely he will be playing on Sunday. "Starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who has been trying to play through a back injury he suffered against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, was not on the practice field at all. … Brown suffered an ankle injury early in Monday's game and gutted through the rest of the evening. After practice, Brown was in the huddle with his teammates, but he was in sandals with a big wrap on his right ankle," Buscagalia wrote . "It wouldn't be stunning if they are playing the long game to give him rest for the back and ankle injuries, given his importance and the Bills' being on a short week. They also have another short week on the horizon, taking on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 12 on Thanksgiving with only three days after their Week 11 game against the Miami Dolphins. Resting Brown could be important. Missing Thursday's practice is usually not a good sign." If Brown can't go, Tylan Grable will start at right tackle again. Grable replaced Brown two weeks ago and started at left tackle a week ago. Given that Buffalo is a huge favorite, resting Brown makes sense to make sure he's healthy for the stretch run. Although the Bills are massive favorites against the Jets, Buffalo isn't overlooking them. Bills head coach Joe Brady believes the Jets pose a challenge for them on defense. So, they have to be smart with the football. "When you look at it, you can get caught up in the records, but the records, I think, always lie to you in the NFL; that's why you never can focus on them," Brady said . "I think it's a really good offense that has been in a lot of games, and there's a lot of one-score games, and you take a couple plays here and there situationally, and the record looks completely different, and people are probably talking about the Jets a little differently. "So it's going to be a huge challenge for us defensively as a football team and a great opportunity for us." The Bills are 8.5-point favorites on the road against the Jets. away.headline: Spitting NFL star claims everyone turned on me in rambling statement after getting cut by Bills
away.blurb: Discarded NFL star CJ Gardner-Johnson finally addressed his release by the Buffalo Bills on Saturday, claiming 'everyone turned on me.' The former Super Bowl champion was axed by Buffalo earlier this month after he was suspended for spitting at an opponent. He had played just six games for the team. Gardner-Johnson was slapped with a one-game ban after he was caught spitting at Las Vegas Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum and tight end Brock Bowers just before halftime of the Bills' Week 6 matchup. The 28-year-old was ejected from the game and the vile incident now sits in history as his final moment in a Bills uniform. He has not yet been signed by another team. Over a week later, the safety posted an emotional message to his Instagram story on Saturday. He wrote: 'In just a couple of weeks, EVERYONE turned on me! No friends, no real support, it sucks we live in a society where one move can cause a downfall to anything! 'If this the last time yall see my face or hear from me it’s cause you don’t understand the person, went through years of pain, alone, suffering trying to fit in, never got the same opportunity everybody else got! 'And when I say same opportunities, just check my history "my attitude and character" my position but no real stories to back that up! It’s ok though as a man I just pray that one day it get better.' In six games for the Bills this season, Gardner-Johnson recorded 26 tackles and one interception. Buffalo was his sixth NFL team in eight seasons. He previously played for New Orleans, Philadelphia, Detroit, Houston and Chicago before signing a one-year contract with the Bills. He was ejected in 2024 while playing for Philadelphia and has been fined numerous times during his NFL career, though he has never been suspended. In the latest incident, cameras had caught him approaching Raiders tight end Bowers for a heated exchange of words – before spitting in his rival's direction. The shocking moment occurred right in front of an official, who quickly flagged the action. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the game soon after and left the field with a bizarre grin on his face. Following the incident, Gardner-Johnson, who won a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles, issued a groveling apology on social media. He wrote: 'I want to take a moment to address my actions and sincerely apologize to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me. 'My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed. The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game.' home.headline: Jets get major Garrett Wilson injury update from Aaron Glenn
home.blurb: His return would put him and Breece Hall on the field together for quarterback Geno Smith, something that hasn’t happened since Week 3. Hall, a running back, rejoined the lineup last week following a five-game absence with an injured quadriceps. Wilson got hurt against Las Vegas in the game before the Kansas City trip. He missed practice entirely the following week, sat out the Chiefs game and was limited in two sessions since. Omar Cooper Jr., a rookie receiver, was limited all week by an ankle injury but should play too. That gives the Jets Wilson, Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams at receiver, with every one of their tight ends available. On defense, edge rusher Joseph Ossai, defensive lineman Harrison Phillips and cornerbacks Jarvis Brownlee Jr. and Nahshon Wright should all be available, per Glenn. Backup linebacker Trevin Wallace won’t play due to a groin injury. Garrett Wilson sits a single concussion protocol step away from returning, and New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn believes the wide receiver will clear it before facing the Buffalo Bills . Wilson leads the 2-7 Jets with 43 catches for 527 yards and three touchdowns, and New York has dropped four straight heading into a Week 10 meeting with a Bills club that shares the league’s top record, 7-1, alongside San Francisco. Glenn explained where things stand with his top wideout. “Garrett still has one more step to go through before he’s cleared,” Glenn said . “And I see that happening.” Asked whether he expected Wilson to suit up against Buffalo, the coach didn’t hedge. “I am confident in that,” Glenn said. Those numbers came amid his frustration over how inconsistently offensive coordinator Frank Reich has used him. Reich and Glenn have both said they’d work on fixing that. Buffalo ranks first leaguewide in scoring and total yards, so New York may need Wilson to help it trade points. New York still has to release one more injury report before the Bills game, and that one will carry official designations. While nobody missed the team's walkthrough, several key contributors are managing injuries, including four offensive linemen who were listed as limited participants. Buffalo's first injury report of Week 10 includes six limited participants and five full participants. The team held a walkthrough on Wednesday, meaning the participation designations are estimates rather than the result of a full practice. The biggest area to watch remains along the offensive line. Alec Anderson, Spencer Brown, Dion Dawkins, and Connor McGovern were all limited Wednesday. Anderson and Brown were listed with ankle injuries, Dawkins with a rib injury, and McGovern with a neck injury. Christian Benford was also limited by a wrist injury. The cornerback dealt with the issue during Monday's game against Minnesota. It caused him to briefly leave the game, and his availability will be worth watching as the week progresses. Tight end Dalton Kincaid rounded out the limited participants, appearing on the report with an ankle injury. Kincaid also briefly left Monday's game after appearing to roll his ankle but returned to finish the contest. It's also important to note that the chest injury he had been listed for in weeks past seems to no longer be an issue. Despite concerns about the limited players, there was some positive news on the defensive side of the ball. Defensive tackle Greg Gaines was a full participant despite dealing with a calf injury that kept him out of the previous two games. Defensive lineman T.J. Sanders was also full with a shoulder injury. Brown and McGovern also appeared on the report, giving the Bills four offensive linemen to monitor heading into the weekend. Guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams was full with back and elbow injuries. Finally, the Bills also have decisions approaching on two players working their way back from injury designations. Defensive back Jordan Hancock, who is returning from injured reserve, and wide receiver Tyrell Shavers, who is returning from the PUP list, were both full participants again on Wednesday. However, Buffalo has not yet made a decision on either player's roster status. The situation is particularly pressing for Shavers. Seattle is coming off a quieter offensive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, but this matchup presents a chance for the Seahawks to get back on track in a big way. The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. Meanwhile, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first NFL start against a Seattle defense that has been one of the toughest units in the league. I expect the Seahawks to take advantage of both matchups. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 4: Jadarian Price scores his first NFL touchdown Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images This could finally be the game when Jadarian Price gets into the end zone for the first time in his NFL career. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. JSN is coming off a relatively quiet performance against the Cardinals, finishing with seven catches for 51 yards without a touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. away.blurb: The Seahawks will be getting a couple of players back from injury for Sunday's game in Las Vegas, with outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu and receiver Rashid Shaheed both ready to return after missing the past two games with ankle and knee injuries, respectively. The Seahawks will still be without four players who also missed last week's game: left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (ribs/quadriceps), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), all of whom were ruled out on Friday's injury report. Cross, who was able to practice Thursday on a limited basis, should be able to make it back after Seattle's Week 11 bye, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. Quarterback Drew Lock was limited all week due to elbow and oblique injuries, as was expected coming into the week, but he has no injury designation, and the plan is still for him to make his second straight start in place of Darnold. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed , who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a personal matter, was back at practice Friday and will play, Macdonald said, clarifying that it was a good personal matter. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and receiver Dont'e Thornton (back), are listed as questionable. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who is dealing with a stinger, was a non-participant for the second day in a row, as were quarterback Sam Darnold and left guard Quenton Nelson , both of whom have already been ruled out of Week 10 by Mike Macdonald. The pool of limited players includes Anthony Bradford (knee), Derick Hall (back) , Drew Lock (right elbow, oblique), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), and Connor O'Toole (foot). Offhand, I would expect all five of those players to play on Sunday, but any injury is noteworthy. Nwosu's return to practice is particularly significant, as he attempted a similar timeline last week with a limited practice on Wednesday before getting banished back to DNP the next two days. Hopefully this time, whatever setback or occurrence caused him to hit the bench doesn't happen and he's able to progress. The other injuries strike me as management ones. home.headline: Seahawks Week 10 injury report vs. Raiders: Leonard Williams injury is good news for Fernando Mendoza
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Leonard Williams against the Las Vegas Raiders , removing a major defensive obstacle for Fernando Mendoza ahead of his first NFL start. Williams missed every practice this week with a stinger and was officially ruled out Friday, leaving Seattle to adjust its defensive front for Sunday's matchup. His absence is one of four confirmed setbacks for the Seahawks. Quarterback Sam Darnold, left tackle Charles Cross and guard Quenton Nelson are also out, creating challenges on both sides of the ball as Seattle heads to Las Vegas. Williams' recovery has not progressed enough for a return to contact. Head coach Mike Macdonald explained Friday that the defensive tackle can move around and maintain his conditioning, but the injury remains an obstacle to playing. Seattle, however, views the unfamiliar quarterback as a preparation challenge of its own. Defensive tackle Byron Murphy II noted the limited professional film available on Mendoza while emphasizing that the rookie can make every throw. Murphy stressed coordinated pressure and communication as priorities. The Seahawks received encouraging news elsewhere up front. Uchenna Nwosu progressed from two limited sessions to full participation Friday and carries no game designation. Brandon Pili also returned to full work after missing Wednesday and Thursday with a back injury, providing available depth without replacing Williams' individual impact. Darnold missed all three practices with rib and quadriceps injuries. Drew Lock is expected to start again despite managing right elbow and oblique issues. Lock remained limited throughout the week but received no game designation. Protecting him becomes more complicated without Cross and Nelson. Cross briefly returned for limited work Thursday before sitting out Friday with his ankle injury. Nelson did not practice all week because of his knee issue. Anthony Bradford offered better news, advancing to full participation Friday after two limited sessions. Derick Hall missed Friday after two limited sessions with a back injury, but he also carries no game designation. That distinction leaves Seattle with four confirmed absences and no additional players officially listed as questionable. home.blurb: Seahawks-Raiders Wednesday injury report: Leonard Williams still out, Rashid Shaheed returns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Seattle released the first of the three weekly injury reports, which is headlined by the health of backup quarterback Drew Lock, who is battling a lingering elbow injury and a new oblique injury. Lock was limited in practice on Wednesday, with head coach Mike Macdonald indicating that the veteran is "making good progress" and may start against the Raiders. Whoever is under center will once again be working with a patchwork offensive line as stars Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross did not practice. Nelson is battling a knee injury that might hold him out for his second straight game while Cross has been out with an ankle injury since Week 7. Backup guard Anthony Bradford continues to be hampered by a knee injury and was limited on Wednesday. On the defensive side, Leonard Williams remains out with a stinger that he suffered against the Kansas City Chiefs, and edge rusher Derick Hall was limited with a new back injury. Both would be a massive loss for the Seahawks front that will hope to ruin Raiders' rookie Fernando Mendoza's debut. It wasn't all negative for the Seahawks' defense, though, as signs are trending positive for edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who was limited with the ankle injury that's held him out of the team's last two games. Jack Freeman · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:29 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Seattle Seahawks emerged victorious in an injury bowl against the Arizona Cardinals last week, and it appears they may have to do it again on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. The ominous messaging leaves the entirety of Seattle on Jalen Milroe watch yet again as the second-year player is the only other healthy quarterback on the Seahawks' 53-man roster and would come in if Lock couldn't play. The Seahawks offense appears to have a weapon returning as wide receiver and kicker returner Rashid Shaheed was a full participant in practice. Shaheed has had a quiet 2026, but remains a key piece to unlocking the Seahawks' offense as the organization is hopeful he emerges as a second option beside Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Meanwhile, the Raiders report was considerably smaller, so it appears they'll be near full-go against their former AFC West rival. For the Seahawks, they will have two more days of practice before setting game designations, so here's to hoping that the report shrinks throughout the week.

The Arizona Cardinals must march the rookie quarterback out to face the Los Angeles Rams (-9.5) and their gruesome twosome of Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett in Week 10. My Rams vs. Cardinals predictions sort out the shifting sands in the NFC West, highlighting some of my best NFL picks for Nov. 15. TOP Pick Rams vs Cardinals prediction: Under 39.5 This total has dropped a touchdown since opening last Sunday night. And it's not just the Arizona Cardinals' QB quandary dragging the number down. Both teams will be without their WR1s, as Los Angeles Rams wideout Puka Nacua and Arizona standout Michael Wilson suffered injuries in Week 9. The cupboard is very bare for Carson Beck , with no Wilson or Kendrick Bourne to throw to, nor does he have RBs Jeremiyah Love and James Conner to help shoulder the offensive load. As for the Rams, their snake-bitten lineup is looking ahead to a much-needed bye in Week 11 . With a spread this size, I expect Los Angeles to try and get up quick and then slow things down in the second half to avoid further casualties. Los Angeles has seen a significant shift in play calling the past three games, upping its run rate from 36% in the first six outings to 48.5% during this current three-game win streak. That's slimmed the Rams' yards per play from 5.9 to 5.2 but upped their average time of possession. Rams vs Cardinals combo A lack of weapons, a rookie QB, and a Rams team trying to get to the bye week without suffering any more hurt. These are all reasons Arizona and Los Angeles stay below the total in Week 10. Blake Corum has scored a touchdown in four straight games, including a receiving TD vs. Arizona in Week 6. He'll get a lot of love in the second half, given the big spread and game script. Tyler Allgeier is now the Cardinals RB1 and is getting a ton of work, with injuries up and down this offense. He's drawn at least three targets in the past three games, and with a rookie QB under center, Allgeier will be a favorite option on short, safe throws. He's seen a spike in carries and has struck for a touchdown in each of those outings. Corum does the bulk of his damage in the second half, providing relief for RB1 Kyren Williams , with four of his five total TDs this season coming in the closing 30 minutes. His lone first-half strike was a 15-yard touchdown reception in the Week 6 upset loss to Arizona. Given the beefy spread and the game-script attached to it, Corum will continue to see touches in the final two frames on Sunday. His touchdown forecasts range from 31% to 50% in Week 10. picks.blurb: A Duel in the Desert: Los Angeles Rams vs Arizona Cardinals Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football live updates Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved RAF Abu Dhabi: Chimaev crushes NFL news, live updates A Duel in the Desert: Los Angeles Rams vs Arizona Cardinals Preview Nov 8, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay sets the play against the Washington Commanders during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Chris Pownall Toussaint Fancher · Last Word on Sports Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:56 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams have an opportunity to avenge their Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. A Duel in the Desert: Los Angeles Rams vs. Arizona Cardinals Preview Los Angeles has dealt with injuries to several star players throughout the season, but last week brought their worst injury yet. Puka Nacua sustained a blow to his knee on the Rams' final offensive play, which left him with sprains to his posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) ,medial collateral ligament (MCL), and a case of turf toe. Now, Los Angeles must survive until Nacua returns. Head coach Sean McVay knows the Rams have what it takes to beat the Cardinals in their second matchup. "One of the calling cards for our group, and is always an expectation, is we play with passion and energy, and I think we would all agree that (the first game against the Cardinals) wasn't quite up to our standards," McVay said . Los Angeles will likely rely on running 13 personnel while several of their best receivers are sidelined with injuries. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford must spread the targets in order to keep Arizona's defense off guard. "It's not difficult to pull the trigger, I trust those guys," Stafford said . Nov 8, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) throws the ball against the Washington Commanders during the third quarter at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images While several receivers are injured, the Rams could also become a more defensively minded team. Los Angeles defensive coordinator Chris Shula has done a great job this year. He knows the defense will need to perform even better than it did when the Rams first played the Cardinals. "We didn't get the win so obviously it wasn't good enough," Shula said . Last time these two teams faced each other, the Rams' defensive unit held the Cardinals to six field goals. Last week, Los Angeles welcomed back Myles Garrett after his time on the injured reserve. He finished the game with three sacks, including a strip sack showing his dominance in a Los Angeles jersey for the first time. Garrett's Week 1 performance left much to be desired, especially since he was playing hurt. His return helped Los Angeles defeat the Washington Commanders 20-13. The team is also hoping to get top cornerback Trent McDuffie back from injury. Los Angeles desperately need McDuffie back if they want to keep their season alive. He has missed the past two games after injuring his back in Week 8. This season, McDuffie has been ranked as the third-best cornerback with an 89.8 rating according to Pro Football Focus (PFF). His pass coverage has been exceptional, and he has lived up to expectations in the first year of his massive $124 million deal . Los Angeles is also without their other top cornerback Jaylen Watson , who is out for the season after undergoing shoulder surgery a few weeks ago. Other cornerbacks Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. have stepped up in his absence, but McDuffie's services are still needed. The Last Word Los Angeles' season could already be over with the number of injuries to key players, but regardless of who's available to play, the Rams must keep pushing for the playoffs. The team is currently riding a three-game winning streak since their loss to the Cardinals. Now, they will have another chance to defeat the Cardinals and former Rams offensive coordinator , Mike LaFleur. The key to this weekend is play-calling. If McVay can keep the Cardinals' defense off balance and use everyone in the pass game, the Rams will be in a strong position to win. Like McVay, Stafford must also be at his best. Coming off an MVP season, Stafford is the glue that must hold the offense together while his best targets are sidelined with injuries. away.headline: Rams injury report: CB Trent McDuffie could return
away.blurb: Edge rusher Myles Garrett did not practice Friday and is listed as questionable after being limited the previous two days, but head coach Sean McVay said, “He's feeling good. It's more of just getting him feeling as good as possible. He's had a really good week, played a bunch of snaps and we expect him to be able to build on that, but we're being smart with him.” The full details of the Rams' final Week 10 injury report are below. After each player’s injury, there is the daily status, which is either no status (NS), did not practice (DNP), limited (LIM) or FULL. Starters are noted with an asterisk. *LG Steve Avila (hamstring): DNP, DNP, DNP TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring/practicing while on injured reserve): DNP, DNP, DNP *TE Davis Allen (oblique): LIM, DNP, LIM *S Kam Curl (toe): DNP, DNP, LIM *OLB Myles Garrett (knee): LIM, LIM, DNP *CB Trent McDuffie (back): DNP, DNP, LIM Asked before practice if he expects McDuffie and Curl to play Sunday, McVay said, “I feel good about Kam and Trent. Those injuries certainly haven't been confined to the offense, but the scale on that side of the ball has been staggering. Wide receiver Davante Adams hasn't played since Week 6, tight end Terrance Ferguson since Week 3. Wide receivers Puka Nacua and Jordan Whittington are freshly on injured reserve. Quarterback Matthew Stafford is dealing with soreness in his throwing elbow. The tight end room is “hanging on by a thread”, according to offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. Left guard Steve Avila's hamstring pull means the plague has spread to the offensive line, too. To be sure, McVay, Scheelhaase and the offensive staff will look for creative ways to use the remaining offensive personnel as they wait to be whole again. But it's the other side of the ball – the defense the Rams (5-4) invested so heavily in this offseason – that will need to carry the team in the meantime, starting Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals (3-6). It wouldn't be the first time this year. The Rams' defense was largely responsible for each of the team's last two wins during this three-game winning streak, holding the Chargers and Commanders to 22 combined points. This offseason, the Rams built a defense that could handle such tasks. It started with extensions last fall for Quentin Lake and Nate Landman , ramped up with the additions of corners Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson and climaxed when the 1-2 pass rush punch of Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald joined the fold. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start.
