I knew that particularly on offense — (with) the defense there’s been a guy here and there, but there’s been some decent continuity over the last month, and I think you guys see that," LaFleur said. Cardinals Coach Said The Quiet Part Out Loud on Carson Beck ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' Monday has taken a steep twist thanks to several significant injuries to their offense, and with news of Gardner Minshew potentially being done for the season, the organization has already targeted their next passer. From ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter: "With veteran QB Gardner Minshew sidelined due to a UCL injury, the Cardinals are signing QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals’ practice squad, per sources. The Cardinals will be Johnson’s 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons." Johnson, a perennial backup veteran quarterback, will be the team's No. 2 quarterback as the Cardinals prepare for their Week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams — who just welcomed Myles Garrett back to the mix with a three-sack performance this Sunday. Minshew was injured on the final play of the second quarter against Seattle. He returned to finish the game but showed obvious discomfort. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck is slated to start for Arizona this week. Johnson, 40 years old, first entered the league as a fifth-round pick in the 2008 NFL Draft. He's played 50 NFL games with 11 starts, most recently starting twice for the Washington Commanders in 2025. In those two games, Johnson completed 34 of 54 passes for 372 yards for one touchdown and two interceptions. He has a 2-9 record as a starter. It was an extremely tough day for the Cardinals, who lost both Minshew and Michael Wilson . Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur says the team has to regroup, even amid the injuries. "I think you see 11 has won more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now and that’s what I meant by that. There’s been a lot of moving parts, and I have to do a better job of stabilizing that to make sure that we don’t have performances like we did yesterday.” The Cardinals recently dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens last week, thinning their quarterback room down to two. With Minshew injured, Beck was the only healthy quarterback on the roster prior to Johnson's signing. home.headline: Arizona Cardinals face quarterback crisis as Gardner Minshew faces potential season-ending injury
home.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur addressed the media on Monday, confirming that Minshew is scheduled for an MRI to determine the full extent of the damage. While the team has not officially ruled the quarterback out for the year, the organization is already preparing for a transition under center. Reports indicate that rookie Carson Beck is the primary candidate to assume the starting responsibilities should Minshew be placed on the sidelines for an extended period. The Arizona Cardinals are confronting a significant roster challenge following reports that starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II has sustained a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing arm. The injury, which occurred during Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks, has raised concerns that the 30-year-old signal-caller may be sidelined for the remainder of the season. The incident took place on the final play of the first half when Minshew was struck while being sacked. Despite the severity of the injury, Minshew returned to the field for the third quarter and completed the game. Following the contest, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that the quarterback is undergoing further medical evaluations, with initial assessments suggesting a recovery period that could span several months. Transition to Rookie Leadership and Roster Adjustments Beck’s path to the starting lineup was cleared earlier this week when the Cardinals traded veteran Jacoby Brissett, effectively elevating the rookie to the backup position. Although Beck has yet to make his regular-season debut, he saw significant action during the preseason Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers, where he completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown. His development was previously hindered by a rib injury, but his recent promotion has increased his involvement in team practices. To bolster the quarterback room, the Cardinals are reportedly moving to sign veteran Josh Johnson from the Cleveland Browns' practice squad. The addition of Johnson provides the team with necessary depth as they navigate the uncertainty surrounding Minshew’s status and prepare for the upcoming stretch of the season. (Tom Fox/Dallas Morning News) SportsDay Staff · Dallas Morning News Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will the Cowboys finally be able to climb back to .500 and pick up their first marquee win of the season? They'll have a massive opportunity to do just that Sunday when the San Francisco 49ers come to AT&T Stadium as the two teams renew their historic rivalry . Dallas enters the game with a 4-5 record and, after the Commanders' win over the Giants on Thursday, a chance to climb even with New York in the win column. Meanwhile, San Francisco enters the game with a 7-1 record and has quickly established itself as one of the NFL's Super Bowl favorites. Can the Cowboys pull off an upset and get their season back on track? The Dallas Morning News ' columnists and beat writers gave their predictions below. Tim Cowlishaw The good news for Dallas is the 49ers can't really take advantage of the Cowboys' challenged secondary because of their injury troubles at wide receiver. The bad news is the 49ers can take advantage of everything else. A team that plays with grit despite its current 7-1 record, San Francisco figures to dominate time of possession with its multi-pronged running attack, and it will take some huge plays from Dak Prescott against the league's No. 3 defense to keep the Cowboys engaged for long in this one. The recipe is there for a Cowboys loss. The Cowboys haven't pieced together back-to-back wins in nearly a year, despite many opportunities along the way. The 49ers might be the class of the NFC, with an offense that continues to score, despite a ton of injuries, and a defense that is as fast as it is physical. Will this be the week the Cowboys finally stack two wins in a row? It's unlikely. 49ers 35, Cowboys 28 You won't find many (any?) realistic NFL fans giving the Cowboys a shot to win this week. Any path to victory would include the 49ers making self-inflicted mistakes and Dallas' offense playing flawlessly. Yes, the Cowboys' offense performs much better at AT&T Stadium, but it still disappears for long stretches during games. Even Brandon Aubrey has struggled to find his range of late. The red-clad fans will have plenty to cheer for in Arlington. Abraham Nudelstejer Given what we've seen this season, this is probably the easiest prediction to make so far. The Cowboys already have lost at home to a team whose season is all but over, and to another that could still reach the playoffs only because of the woeful state of its division. There is no tangible evidence of improvement that would justify picking Dallas to beat a squad that, with just one loss all year, appears destined to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl. The best Dallas can realistically hope for is to put up a spirited fight and begin preparing for next week's game. 49ers 34, Cowboys 13 Kevin Sherrington Jerry Jones did the right thing by not mortgaging any more of his future to try to save this season, and this game against the 49ers should do nothing but affirm that decision. The Cowboys won't hang 500 yards on the 49ers like they did the Colts. San Francisco has the third-best defense in the NFL, meaning Dak Prescott can't hope to outscore them. 49ers 31, Cowboys 24 Calvin Watkins If the postseason started today, the 49ers would be the No. 1 seed. The Cowboys? Well, you know what's happening with them. If the Cowboys want to get back into the playoff chase, and that's winning the NFC East, beating the 49ers is a good start. It's a difficult task considering how good the 49ers are on defense (ranked third in total defense) so the Cowboys' offense will have to be near-perfect. That's hard to do. The rookie also handled double-digit rushing attempts in the season opener against the Los Angeles Rams, finishing with 65 yards on 14 carries. McCaffrey’s workload remains below last season’s pace. He finished the 2025 regular season with 311 carries and 102 receptions across 17 starts, totaling 2,126 yards from scrimmage and 17 touchdowns. He won the AP Comeback Player of the Year award. Through eight games this year, McCaffrey has 138 touches for 727 yards from scrimmage. His receiving role remains far larger than Black’s, who has three catches for four yards. McCaffrey caught nine passes against Washington and six against Atlanta before San Francisco’s bye. He has scored at least one touchdown in seven straight games, including two-touchdown performances against Miami, Washington and Las Vegas. That honor goes to DaRon Bland, who was a surprise addition to Friday's injury report due to an ankle injury. He practiced in full on Wednesday and Thursday, yet was downgraded to limited on Friday, so it feels like his status is in real doubt, although we don't know much about what actually happened. home.headline: Dallas Cowboys Add CB Help Amid Joey Porter Jr. Uncertainty For 49ers Game
home.blurb: The 49ers come into town as slight 3.5-point favorites on the road, but with how unpredictable Dallas has been all season, you can never count anything out. We will find out our answers to all of the questions when the Cowboys and 49ers kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX, in America's Game of the Week. Kevin Burkhardt will be on play-by-play and Tom Brady will serve as analyst, while Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi provide updates from the sideline throughout the evening. In less than 24 hours, the Dallas Cowboys will be returning to the field at AT&T Stadium for a crucial clash with the NFC rival San Francisco 49ers in Week 10. Dallas has an opportunity to continue closing in on the NFC East lead with an upset win. Ahead of Sunday's game, the Cowboys made a flurry of roster moves, which included moving breakout star running back Tyler Goodson to injured reserve with an ACL and MCL sprain. To fill the void on the active roster left by Goodson heading to IR, the team officially elevated Israel Abanikanda to the game-day roster . But Dallas wasn't done yet, because they added tight end and cornerback help, while activating another former start from IR/DTR. A full look at Saturday's roster moves can be seen below. Dallas Cowboys Add CB Reinforcements Amid Saturday Activity With the status of star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. up in the air, the Cowboys elevated cornerback Derion Kendrick from the practice squad. Porter has been battling a nagging foot injury , which kept him sidelined in Week 9, but there is some hope he will be ready to go. Now, the Cowboys have some extra depth. In addition to the Kendrick move, the Cowboys activated defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard from Reserve/Injured-DFR, signed tight end James Mitchell to the active roster from the practice squad, and waived outside linebacker Tyus Wheat . Whether any of the new additions are called upon on Sunday afternoon to play a significant role in the gameplan remains to be seen, but you can never have too much depth, especially against a team of the 49ers' caliber. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pittsburgh won the first matchup between the two teams back in Week 3 Getty Images The 10th Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will conclude with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals battling for first place in the AFC North division. Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh. Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown. Where to watch Bengals vs. Steelers live When: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Where: Paycor Stadium -- Cincinnati, Ohio TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3.5, O/U 47.5 (via DraftKings ) Bengals vs. Steelers: Need to know Last time we met The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-27 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. Reasons for success Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally. Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe . Prediction, pick This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night. In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. He also leads the team in red zone targets, nearly double those of Tee Higgins: 13 to seven. First touchdown scorer pick: Chase Brown The numbers don't look good at first glance for Chase Brown , with just one touchdown all season, which came all the way back in Week One, but I urge you to look past that. Positive regression is coming his way because he's been very efficient lately. Last week, he finished with +11 rushing yards over expected . Samaje Perine doesn't look like much of a factor either; even if he had an increased workload last week, he simply isn't as efficient. The Steelers' run defense is good, but with Burrow playing at MVP levels and the passing game thriving, it might open the box slightly, giving Brown some chances. Long-shot touchdown pick: Joe Burrow As much as I think Brown will score on Sunday, I can't help but think it's his quarterback who offers the best long shot on the board. We've seen the Cincinnati Bengals QB pick up three rushing touchdowns this season , including one TD in each of the past weeks. He's had five rushing attempts inside the 10 this season, which doesn't sound like much, but it's one more than Perine, who is a 29% chance to score, and only three less than Brown, who is nearly a pick'em. Steelers vs Bengals touchdown combo The Chase-Higgins combination is arguably the best receiving duo in football, and they've already racked up 13 touchdowns this season. In eight games, they've had four games in which they've both found the end zone. With Burrow continuing to put up great numbers, I'm keen to back them finding the end zone together again, much like they did when they played the Steelers in Week Three. It is huge matchup in the AFC North, where everyone is still in contention. These two teams are currently tied at the top with twin 6-2 records. Here is my SGP for Sunday’s primetime festivities, which get underway at 8:20 pm ET on NBC. Also be sure to check out our full Steelers vs Bengals predictions . Bengals ML (-180) Over 49.5 (-108) Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) Tee Higgins to score a touchdown (+120) Parlay odds: +625 Part of the value in a Same Game Parlay, of course, is that all of its components can be correlated if you so choose. That is the entire plan here, as Cincinnati receiver Tee Higgins having a big night would obviously work well with a win by the Bengals and plenty of points being scored. Let’s break down each of the three legs. Pittsburgh prevailed 30-27 in the first head-to-head showdown on September 27, but I’m not too concerned. The Steelers have swept the Bengals in a regular-season series only once since 2019. Aaron Rodgers’ squad overachieved in the first half of this season, but the first nine weeks were hardly convincing. Cincinnati, on the other hand, was mightily impressive en route to its six victories. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are looking unstoppable. Even the defense has become an average unit – and average means good by the Bengals’ standards on that side of the ball. I’m not willing to give more than a field goal in this AFC North rivalry matchup (or really in any game involving two teams from this division), but the Bengals should be able to win it outright. This correlates nicely with the Bengals on the money line. After all, you can be almost certain that a whole bunch of points will be scored if the game is played at Cincinnati’s pace. Pittsburgh, of course, would much rather play more of a defensive slog. The first meeting between these two teams in 2026 resulted in 57 points, obviously an encouraging sign for another over on Sunday. The Bengals have not slowed down, either. In fact, they have only been getting better and better. Burrow and company have put 31, 35, 43 and 34 points on the board in their last four outings. Although Cincy’s defense has stepped up in recent weeks, keep in mind that this is a unit that got torched for 36 points by the lowly Titans earlier this month. The Bengals also watched the Steelers churn out 7.0 yards per play in this season’s first head-to-head matchup. Cincinnati ranks dead last in the entire NFL in opponents’ yards per rush (5.0), so Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren can be expected to go borderline crazy in this one. He turned 17 attempts into 127 yards against Cincy earlier this year. Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) and to score a touchdown (+120) Higgins has been on a heater of late – and really this entire season. The Clemson product has caught 48 of 67 targets for 758 yards and six touchdowns. He has produced at least 148 yards in three of the last five games and has scored five touchdowns in the past three weeks. Yes – five touchdowns in the past three weeks. Burrow is playing like an MVP candidate (if not even the favorite) and Chase always demands a ton of attention from opposing defenses. Elite cornerback Jamel Dean will likely be on Chase for the most part, which means things could open up for Higgins. When these two teams faced each other back in Week 3, Higgins made six receptions on seven targets for 90 yards and one TD. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football live updates Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved RAF Abu Dhabi: Chimaev crushes NFL news, live updates Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown Alex Frank · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:05 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is as big of a home game as it gets for the Cincinnati Bengals . It's mid-November, against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and first place in the AFC North is on the line. Both the Bengals and Steelers are 6-2 and have both won four straight games. Not to mention, these two teams have already played this season. It was in Week 3, with the Steelers winning 30-27 in Pittsburgh. Right now on FanDuel , the Bengals are 3.5-point favorites next Sunday night. The Bengals' moneyline is -200, while the Steelers' is at +168. The over/under is at 47.5. Sunday night could be an extremely physical game. It's an AFC North rivalry with sole possession of first place in the division at stake. Also, it's the Bengals and Steelers. That's all you need to know for the potential level of physicality. Pittsburgh stole the first game against the Bengals, aided by two Bengals turnovers in the fourth quarter that included Joe Burrow getting strip-sacked with the Bengals on the edge of field goal range in the final minute. The Bengals never ran an offensive play with the lead in that game, but there were some great performances from their star players. Joe Burrow was 28/37 for 282 yards and three touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase caught nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins hauled in six passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also caught a 25-yard touchdown on 4th&2 early in the fourth quarter. For the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns, while Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries. Eight different players caught a pass for the Steelers, with Darnell Washington leading the way with 67 receiving yards on three receptions. Roman Wilson, D.K. Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek each caught a touchdown for the Steelers. Rodgers currently has 1,871 passing yards and 13 touchdowns on the season, but he's also thrown six interceptions and is completing just 60.8 percent of his passes. Warren has 704 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Washington and fellow tight end Pat Friermuth lead the Steelers with three and four touchdowns, respectively. T.J. Watt, as of Sunday night, leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks, and he also has nine tackles for loss. Cornerback Jamel Dean also has three forced fumbles. Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt off the stat sheet in that game, which bodes well going into Sunday night. The Bengals' offense scored on five of their eight drives in the first meeting in Week 3, gaining 352 yards of offense and rushing for 83 yards on 18 carries. Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries.

away.headline: Steelers activate Derick Harmon from IR, add Pat Freiermuth to injury report
away.blurb: Harmon had missed the past four games because of a knee injury suffered early during an Oct. 1 loss at the Cleveland Browns. Harmon was cleared to return to practice this week and after making it through sessions in a limited capacity Wednesday and Thursday, he practiced fully Friday. Harmon had entered the weekend listed as questionable to play in Cincinnati on the injury report. Harmon was one of two defensive tackles on IR, joining veteran Sebastian Joseph-Day, who remains out because of a triceps ailment. In other news Saturday, tight end Pat Freiermuth was added to the injury report and given a questionable designation because of illness. Harmon missed the minimum four games required by rule of an IR stint. The Steelers' first-round pick last year, Harmon has 12 tackles and 1 1/2 sacks in three-plus games this season and has 39 tackles and 4 ½ sacks over 16 games in his NFL career. "We've had to have a lot of guys step up," veteran Cameron Heyward said of the defensive line corps. "I thought Yahya Black, Keeanu Benton, even (rookie Gabriel Rubio) and (undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity) have really stepped up in that time, and that just adds to our rotation and allows us to be able to be interchangeable, and it should pay dividends on Sunday." The winner of the 8:20 p.m. kickoff game between the Steelers (6-2) and Bengals (6-2) takes over sole possession of first place in the AFC North. In the corresponding roster move Saturday, the Steelers waived cornerback Terell Smith. Smith signed with the Steelers on Oct. 6 but was a healthy inactive for the ensuing three games before dressing and playing on special teams only during the Steelers' most recent game Nov. 1. Freiermuth has five touchdowns this season (one rushing, four receiving), tied for the fourth-most among NFL tight ends. He has six touchdowns in 11 career games against the Bengals. If Freiermuth can't play, veteran Robert Tonyan would serve as the complement to Darnell Washington for the Steelers at tight end. away.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . home.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
home.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . For up-to-date Steelers coverage, including any roster news and injury updates, follow us on X @TheSteelersWire and give our Facebook page a like. The the Ravens are fresh off a loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football, in which they started third-string rookie Joe Fagnano due to injuries plaguing Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The Ravens are expected to start Jacoby Brissett after acquiring him in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals for a fourth-round pick. The game against the Ravens will mark the team's first game facing off against former defensive coordinator Jesse Minter, who became the Ravens' head coach during the offseason. picks.blurb: 2. Justin Herbert avoided a fracture: Now, can the Chargers protect him? Imaging came back negative on the middle finger of his non-throwing hand, and Herbert said he expects to play. The bigger matchup concern is that Houston sacked him a career-high eight times. Baltimore can make this a long night if the Chargers keep putting him in third-and-long. 3. Keep an eye on Kyle Hamilton's hip: If Baltimore's safety is limited or unavailable, that could give Herbert more room to attack the middle of the field with quick throws. That's one way for the Chargers to take pressure off their offensive line, especially if Ladd McConkey is healthy enough to handle his usual workload. 4. Something's gotta give: Right? Los Angeles is 0-8, the NFL's only remaining winless team. Baltimore has dropped four in a row to plummet to the bottom of the AFC North after a 4-1 start. Someone will win in primetime. Unless there's a tie. 5. Home is for the birds: Baltimore is 2-11 ATS at home since the start of last season, failing to cover by 9.7 points per game, according to Evan Abram's NFL betting primer. The Ravens have failed to cover the spread in eight straight home games, which is the longest home against-the-spread skid in franchise history. 6. Primetime Herbert: With Justin Herbert, the Chargers are 18-8 ATS in primetime night games, winning six in a row outright since 2024. Am I really going to change course now just because Lamar Jackson's unavailable? No chance. Jacoby Brissett will make his first Ravens start and it remains to be seen how good he'll be but he's absolutely an immediate upgrade on rookie Joe Fagnano and likely journeyman Tyler Huntley as well. Brissett's used to a heavy passing load and maybe that will bring Zay Flowers back to life. As for the Bolts, Justin Herbert plans to play after hurting a finger on his non-throwing hand. He just took eight sacks in Houston and Baltimore's defense is fully capable of frustrating him as well. Plus, Ladd McConkey still isn't right. This may not get ugly, but it won't end well for Los Angeles. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Chargers 17-16 Is it time? The Bolts finally ended their 37-possession touchdown drought last week, and maybe the long-sought first win could be in sight. That might seem like a stretch against most teams, but facing the floundering Ravens gives Los Angeles a chance for another breakthrough. Getting Jacoby Brissett in the fold might raise Baltimore's floor a bit, but this feels like another team that's fighting against its emerging reality of a lost season. L.A. gets to take on old friend and current Ravens head coach Jesse Minter on 'Monday Night Football' in what might be one of the worst games of the season. The Ravens are down to Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, who is tasked with guiding an already uninspiring offense. The Chargers are desperate for a win and this isn't a Ravens defense to be worried about. The stars are aligning, even though we won't be seeing many on the field. away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season." Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson's surgery happened last week so based on the estimated recovery time of six to 10 weeks, he could potentially be back on the field before the regular season ends. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Nov. 13 that Jackson's recovery timeline was "challenging to predict" after he underwent surgery to address a dislocated and broken right thumb. A six-week recovery would have Jackson back around Week 15 when the Ravens play the Pittsburgh Steelers. The full 10-week timeline would give him a chance to play in Week 18, also against the Steelers. In addition to his hand injury, Jackson also missed three games earlier in the year after suffering a high ankle sprain. In five games, he played just 14 full quarters and threw for 961 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and another score. In the wake of Jackson's injury, the Ravens traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to make his first start for the team against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. At 4-5, Baltimore has work to do if it hopes to make the playoffs. The Ravens will likely remain cautious with Jackson's recovery, making the acquisition of Brissett a critical move as they look to snap their four-game losing streak going into Monday night.

home.headline: Ravens get devastating update on Lamar Jackson’s status
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens offered a clearer picture of Lamar Jackson’s recovery Friday but stopped short of setting a return date for their franchise quarterback. “Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Jackson injured his throwing hand on Baltimore’s first offensive play against Buffalo on November 1. His right hand struck Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau as he attempted a throw, immediately ending his return to the lineup. He had already missed three games with an ankle injury. Related Articles Kirk Cousins’ Vikings Return Comes With an Emotional Twist In a statement released by the team, head coach Jesse Minter said injuries like Jackson’s broken and dislocated thumb typically require six to 10 weeks to heal when surgery is necessary. The update leaves Baltimore preparing for an extended stretch without the two-time NFL MVP as it tries to reverse a four-game losing streak. “Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8,” Minter said. Minter described a typical healing window rather than announcing Jackson would miss another six to 10 weeks beginning Friday. The statement did not specify a target game or establish when that recovery window began. The Ravens’ quarterback problems worsened that afternoon when Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the Buffalo game and started the following Thursday against Jacksonville. Baltimore lost those games 36-10 and 33-10, respectively, falling to 4-5. Following the loss, the Ravens made a trade to acquire Jacoby Brissett from Arizona on November 6. The veteran is preparing to make his first Baltimore start Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) while learning a new offense on an accelerated schedule. “It’s definitely a crash course. No question,” Brissett said Thursday. Baltimore has scored no more than 13 points in any game during its four-game skid. Brissett’s immediate assignment is to restore enough offensive consistency to stop that slide. Jackson has not abandoned the possibility of returning this season. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport previously reported that he told teammates he intended to come back, although his recovery and Baltimore’s ability to remain competitive will shape that possibility. The Ravens need to keep their season alive while Jackson recovers. That responsibility now falls to Brissett, whose first start Monday offers Baltimore a chance to end its four-game skid and give its injured quarterback something to come back to.
